racecards.race_name: Dunraven Windows Miss Millbrook Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.owner: Middleham Park Racing & M & L Sainsbury
runners.comment: Scored comfortably at Plumpton; outstayed over 3m since; major player back down in trip
runners.spotlight: Scored comfortably at Plumpton (2m4f, soft) on second attempt under rules; outstayed by the winner, who is useful, over 3m at Doncaster since; may still have more to offer and holds major claims back down in trip.

stable_tour.quote: He's a really good-looking horse and he's coming along nicely. He had two runs in Irish point-to-points and was placed. He's a big, solid chaser who won't be for top of the ground, that's for sure. He'll start over hurdles. 21-10-25

runners.comment: 0-13 over hurdles but is in form, runner-up over C&D last time; fighting chance
runners.spotlight: Chase winner for previous yard; 0-13 over hurdles but is in form for new stable, having finished second in handicaps on last two outings, latest over C&D (good to soft) behind easy winner; fighting chance at the weights.

stable_tour.quote: He regressed at Stratford last time but did have ulcers, which we're treating, and you should see something like his previous Chepstow form, or better, when he's out next. He'll progress. 12-11-24

runners.comment: Chance partly depends on how well he responds to fitting of tongue-tie
runners.spotlight: Beaten long way over 2m5f at Ludlow, failing to build on his Irish point effort; chance partly depends on how well he responds to fitting of tongue-tie.

runners.comment: Solid contender who has consistent form figures; had wind surgery since last run
runners.spotlight: Weakened into third at Plumpton (2m4f) last time but still has consistent overall form figures, which now read 32333, and subsequent physical tweak (wind surgery) may enable him to finish better; solid chance.

stable_tour.quote: There's nothing flashy about him but when you get to the end of your work he's always there. He was third in a point-to-point last April before we bought him and the form of that race seems to be working out well. 05-11-25

runners.comment: Poor claims on his two rules efforts
runners.spotlight: Holds poor claims on his two rules efforts and is likely one for handicaps later on.

runners.comment: Wind surgery before 4th in these cheekpieces in a maiden at Warwick (2m3f, good) yesterday
runners.spotlight: Irish point winner who was fifth on first two starts under rules, weakening over 2m7f at Chepstow on second occasion; had wind surgery before his fourth in these cheekpieces in a maiden at Warwick (2m3f, good) yesterday, which he needs to improve on.

stable_tour.quote: He was bought at the Cheltenham sale in February after staying on strongly to win his point-to-point. He came highly recommended by Sam Curling and Derek O'Connor, and looks like a proper three-mile chaser. 18-11-25

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Brian Davies
runners.comment: His completions comprise a point win and heavy defeat
runners.spotlight: Not a particularly solid option, with his two completions comprising an Irish point success and heavy defeat in latest hurdles attempt.

runners.comment: Juvenile hurdler who kept on for third upped to 2m3f last time; may show progress
runners.spotlight: Juvenile hurdler whose reasonably consistent form features an autumn win; keeping-on third upped to 2m3f in Taunton handicap (good) most recently; may show progress kept to this distance; respected.

stable_tour.quote: My daughter Megan bought him off the Flat in Ireland, where he showed plenty of ability in middle-distance maidens. He's shown real enthusiasm for jumping from day one and ran respectably on his debut in quite a hot little event at Chepstow; the winner, Ammes, is probably very good. He's sure to come on enormously for the run and should win his juvenile hurdles. 04-11-25

runners.breeder: Mrs P Bailey And Miss S Bailey
runners.owner: Mrs P And Miss S Bailey
runners.comment: Trailed home last of seven in Uttoxeter bumper
runners.spotlight: Trailed home last of seven in Uttoxeter bumper for an inauspicious debut; needs a huge step forward.

runners.comment: Far from solid on form
runners.spotlight: Far from solid on form; beaten long way at Chepstow (2m7f) on stable/hurdles debut most recently.

racecards.verdict: The 4yo TREASURE PLANET may be capable of progress at this sort of distance and gets the vote ahead of Piping Rock.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Quay Item,  Beau Quali, 3/1 Piping Rock,  Treasure Planet, 16/1 Vanderflier, 33/1 Drumlee Orders,  Yellow Warning, 50/1 Shuil Rocco,  The Last Promise, 100/1 Equity Release

racecards.race_name: Sun Trade Windows Final Pride Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Trip, ground and mark are all fine, but has a listless recent return run to forgive.
runners.spotlight: Chasing career highlights include a C&D novice handicap and the same Cheltenham April 3m2f event two years running, all on good; 3lb below his last winning mark, but has a listless recent return run to forgive.

quotes.race: Weatherite Air Conditioning Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was important to win for Paddy. Out of his three rides this was the least likely to win but fair play to Sally [Randell, assistant] and people at home because they said Manothepeople was in great form. He was teed up for this. What a way to go out - Fergal O'Brien, trainer.

quotes.race: Follow Vickers.Bet On Twitter Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: You never expect a performance like that first time over fences, but Manofthepeople was very good and got a lovely positive ride. His schooling has been good and he showed a lot of promise last season. He took a while to get going, but Paddy was always sweet on him. We haven't got any plans, but he liked that ground - Fergal O'Brien, trainer.

runners.comment: Can uphold Wincanton form over Loup De Maulde despite rise to a new career-high mark.
runners.spotlight: Chasing record reads 3-6 following this month's 5l defeat of Loup De Maulde at Wincanton (3m1f, good; RPR 128), and although taking him to a new career-high mark the 4lb rise for that doesn't look an overreaction; no track or going issues, and case looks solid once more.

quotes.race: Bridles New Luxury Care Home Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: You have to basically hold Broomfield Cave's hand on the first circuit as he takes his time to warm up. Once he's got his eye in, he's fine, and that was the best he's jumped in the straight. He loves to spring off this better ground and he could never get going in the soft ground at Doncaster last time - Bradley Harris, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He finished second and then first on his last two runs over fences, then had a year off with a bit of an injury. He's in good order now and I thought he galloped well when we took him for an away day. He'll be back out in a staying chase when we get some decent ground. 12-11-25

He won last time out on Boxing Day at Wincanton. The third horse, Jupiter Allen, came out and won again last week, so the form is working out well. The ground would just be a little bit soft for him at present, but once we get a bit of proper good to soft ground again he'll be out. He's a nice staying chaser and there'll be plenty more to come from him. 04-02-26

runners.comment: Saw out 3m better last time (good), but defeats off marks in the 120s keep adding up.
runners.spotlight: Last month's near-5l third at Kempton was his most convincing effort to date both over 3m and on good ground, but also took his record in handicaps off marks in the 120s to 0-8; still needs to find a bit more.

runners.breeder: S C E A De Maulde Et Al

prev_owners.owner: R J Bedford & All Stars Sports Racing

runners.comment: 5l behind Broomfields Cave latest (3m1f); all wins gained at sharper tracks than Chepstow.
runners.spotlight: Not an unlucky loser, but may have run Broomfields Cave closer at Wincanton latest without pecking two out (3m1f, good); respected now back on track, though notably remains winless around a galloping track.

stable_tour.quote: He improved 34lb for us last season, winning four races, and he's very consistent. He had a little bit of a setback this season but he ran in a Pertemps qualifier the other day at Huntingdon, finishing second, and it was great to get him qualified. If he goes up in the weights a bit he might have a chance of getting into the final and it would be great to have a Cheltenham Festival runner. He'd be competitive and might finish fifth or sixth. 01-02-24

runners.breeder: E A R L Elevage De Busset & Patrice Gom
runners.owner: H Stephen Smith & The Gabbertas Family
runners.comment: Just held on to land Uttoxeter Class 4 latest (good to soft); handles sound surface also.
runners.spotlight: Right back to form on last month's second start after 16 months out, just holding on in a Uttoxeter Class 4 (3m, good to soft); form of that win remains untested, but 4lb rise probably fair; effective on good also.

runners.comment: This is his time of year, but was an early casualty on recent first outing since May 2025.
runners.spotlight: Last four victories all gained over Ffos Las's 3m4f trip in April or May (good, good to soft); present attainment level is conjectural, having survived just two fences on his recent first outing since last May.

quotes.race: Potters Canter Carpet West Wales National Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Amateur just didn't jump at Exeter but some intensive schooling and taking him to Henrietta Knight's has proved more than worthwhile. He's always had the ability and he needs the trip of these marathon races. We'd have liked to have got him in the Scottish National, but that could be one for next year hopefully - we'll have plenty of fun with him - John Flint, trainer.

quotes.race: MansionBet's Best Odds Guaranteed Mandarin Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: I didn't want to be in front too soon, but I had one to aim at and Amateur was very brave at the last and put his head down. You could see as soon as he hit the front, he started to look about so I just kept him up to his work. He travelled really well and he hurdled through a couple of fences, but as soon as he made the mistake he was back on the bit. We went very quick and stayed going on that ground. - Jamie Bargary, rider

racecards.verdict: A 4lb rise could have been far worse for BROOMFIELDS CAVE, and he's narrowly preferred over fellow last-time scorer Inflexible.
racecards.betting_forecast: 13/8 Broomfields Cave, 7/2 Loup De Maulde,  Inflexible, 6/1 Charles Ritz, 13/2 Manothepeople, 25/1 Amateur

racecards.race_name: Braceys My Coranna Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div I)

runners.comment: His dam is from a useful family but he was tailed off on his two completed starts
runners.spotlight: His dam is from a useful family but he was tailed off on his first two starts and an early faller at Ffos Las 12 days ago.

runners.comment: Ran okay on debut in bumper at Sedgefield but well beaten on his three runs since
runners.spotlight: Ran okay when fourth of six on debut in bumper at Sedgefield in December but well beaten on his three runs since, the last two being over hurdles.

runners.comment: Half-brother to useful Perfect Myth but tailed off at 100-1 on last month's belated debut
runners.spotlight: Half-brother to the useful Perfect Myth but he was tailed off at 100-1 on last month's belated debut at Wincanton (1m7f, good).

runners.comment: 6-21 in points; makes rules debut at age of nine but in a race lacking depth
runners.spotlight: 6-21 in points and in good heart in that sphere of late; makes rules debut at age of nine but in a race lacking depth; could have a part to play.

runners.comment: 0-8 but placed on last three starts and he's high on the list in this modest contest
runners.spotlight: 0-8 but placed over hurdles on his last three starts (2m, soft/good to soft) and that puts him high on the list in a race that might not take much winning; ran well on good ground in a bumper.

runners.comment: Makes stable debut after absence but one of the likelier winners judged on Irish form
runners.spotlight: Three-time Flat winner who has also shown promise over hurdles; well beaten in this code last May and bought out of Denis Hogan's yard for £17,000 later that month; absent since but he's one of the likelier winners if at the top of his game on this comeback and stable debut; watch the betting.

runners.owner: Andrew McGladdery And Park Lodge Stables
runners.comment: Encouraging run on the first of his two hurdle starts; went close on the Flat last time
runners.spotlight: Fairly encouraging fifth of 18 on hurdle debut at Wincanton (1m7f, soft) in December; a lesser run followed at Lingfield (2m, soft) but he's since gone close on the Flat at Kempton (2m, AW), in February; also effective on good ground on the Flat; he's one to consider.

runners.comment: Third in a point in January but tailed off subsequently on her first two runs over hurdles
runners.spotlight: Displayed ability when third in a point in January but tailed off subsequently on her first two runs over hurdles.

runners.comment: Tailed off in both bumpers and same outcome when 125-1 for recent hurdle debut over C&D
runners.spotlight: Related to winners but tailed off in both bumpers and same outcome when 125-1 for recent hurdle debut over C&D (good to soft).

runners.comment: Third in a point in December but pulled up at 33-1 on recent hurdle debut at Newton Abbot
runners.spotlight: Third in a point (3m, yielding to soft) in December on her second start; however, pulled up at 33-1 on hurdle debut at Newton Abbot (2m5f, good) ten days ago and needs to be an entirely different proposition today.

runners.owner: Mrs H Watson & Mrs Carol Lee
runners.comment: 32l third behind two useful sorts over C&D on second hurdle start; this is weaker
runners.spotlight: Progressive on the Flat last year; tailed off on hurdle debut at Stratford last month before 32l third over this C&D (good to soft) three weeks ago, behind two useful sorts; this race should take a lot less winning.

runners.comment: Modest maiden on Flat and soundly beaten at 100-1 on last month's hurdle debut at Taunton
runners.spotlight: Modest maiden on the Flat and soundly beaten at 100-1 on last month's hurdle debut at Taunton (2m, good); improvement is needed.

runners.comment: Soundly beaten last time but could come good for his top yard at some point
runners.spotlight: Soundly beaten sixth of 12 at Huntingdon (2m, good) last month and he needs a bigger performance today; however, he showed some promise when third of eight on hurdle debut at Taunton (2m3f, heavy), when fading late on, and he could come good for his top yard at some point.

stable_tour.quote: He's come from France after a run in an AQPS bumper and he finished second. We'll probably go for a bumper to start with, but he jumps very well. 21-10-25

prev_owners.owner: Valmont, M V Magnier,T Magnier & P Shanahan

runners.comment: Became disappointing on the Flat and no threat on h'dle debut, but could build on that run
runners.spotlight: After showing promise he became disappointing during his short Flat career, and he was beaten 19l when fourth of six on his recent hurdle debut at Fakenham (2m, good); however, that was his first run since last November and it's possible he'll get closer to the target today.

racecards.verdict: Three-time Flat winner BOTH OF US was behind two useful opponents when a 32l third over C&D this month and faces nothing of their ilk.

racecards.race_name: Braceys My Coranna Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race) (Div II)

runners.comment: Smart Flat horse but well beaten last two starts; fascinating runner on stable/hdles debut
runners.spotlight: Really smart Flat campaigner although he was susceptible to the odd aberration; in fine form as recently as last April, when just denied in valuable 1m6f Musselburgh handicap, but last two starts for Karl Burke showed the other side of his coin and left that yard for 21,000gns in November; still rates a fascinating hurdles debutant with the market potentially offering significant clues.

quotes.race: William Hill Epic Value Handicap
quotes.quote: Aimeric is a fun handicapper. He's going up in the ratings, so they could have a crack at something else, but he is what he is. The quicker the better for him. I had to ride him slightly differently, he prefers to not get there too early but they can get away from you down the hill here. He's always had ability, he just needs proper summer ground - James Doyle, rider.

quotes.race: William Hill Silver Cup Handicap
quotes.quote: Aimeric ran well at Ascot but got boxed in on the rail and didn't get a clear run. Then at Newmarket they had a thunderstorm and the rain ruined the ground for him. He likes top-of-the-ground - he's a good mover. He's got his confidence and his mojo back. He'll get better with age -  Jack Mitchell, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: I don't know how much improvement he's got in him but I hope we can place him to win a race or two in the summer. He appreciates fast ground. He could start at York in a mile-and-a-half handicap next month. 25-04-24

He was one of Sheikh Obaid's horses who was with Karl Burke and hasn't run for us yet. He's rated 107 on the Flat and is a seven-year-old but he's going novice hurdling. He's schooled very well and we like him, so you'll see him in the next couple of weeks. He's going to be a good fun project for those northern novice hurdles and has so much ability he should be able to win a couple at least. 04-03-26

runners.comment: Ability on bumper debut but disappointed after; may get back on track switched to hurdles
runners.spotlight: Displayed ability on bumper debut at Warwick (2m, good to soft) in December but disappointed in two subsequent starts; has winning hurdlers in the family so may get back on track switched to this sphere.

stable_tour.quote: He'll run in a bumper at Plumpton on December 1. He's a nice horse who showed some form in a point-to-point. He's not going to go bang in a bumper - he's very green and mentally very backward - but I think he could do some good stuff with a couple of runs under his belt. 01-12-25

runners.comment: No immediate promise when 22-1 and weakening to beat one home in October bumper
runners.spotlight: No immediate promise when 22-1 and weakening quickly to beat one home in October Worcester bumper; hurdles debut.

runners.comment: Outpaced in one bumper; pedigree suggests he'll do better over jumps; hurdles debut
runners.spotlight: 9-1 and outpaced when fifth of seven on bumper debut at Exeter (good) last month; pedigree suggests he'll do better over jumps but probably over further.

runners.comment: Didn't go unbacked before bad mistake and unseat early 12 days ago; market might help
runners.spotlight: Hint of ability on February's hurdling debut and he didn't go unbacked before a bad mistake and unseating early at Wincanton 12 days ago; market might help.

runners.comment: Can't be recommended on his outings in a bumper or maiden and novice; wind surgery
runners.spotlight: Can't be recommended on his outings in a bumper or maiden and novice; has twice been handy before weakening so wind surgery might have helped.

runners.comment: Looked to need the experience on bumper debut; may do better now switched to hurdles
runners.spotlight: Dam was prolific across both codes and disciplines; looked to need the experience when midfield on bumper debut at Taunton (good to soft) in February; may do better on this first go over hurdles.

runners.comment: Big defeats in a bumper and two novices; probably more one for handicaps
runners.spotlight: Big defeats in a bumper and two novices; probably more one for handicaps.

runners.comment: Sets the standard on last of four starts in Ireland; much respected on stable debut
runners.spotlight: Inconsistent at big prices in four Irish hurdling starts but her fourth of 12 at Fairyhouse (2m4f, soft) in January sets the standard; secured for £22,000 a fortnight later; also ran creditably on better ground in November and she's much respected on this stable debut.

runners.comment: Might be one for further once handicapping but he's not entirely ruled out
runners.spotlight: Not disgraced on second bumper start and she plugged on for a very modest third at Stratford (good; first-time cheekpieces) on hurdling debut last month; again outpaced when fifth over C&D (also 2m, good to soft) a fortnight ago; cheekpieces removed for this third go over hurdles and while not dismissed she'll likely do better up in trip once handicapping.

prev_owners.owner: M & M Racing, Paul Byrne And Partner

runners.comment: Not disgraced when fourth on stable/hurdles debut; might have a say
runners.spotlight: Win on the Flat came at 1m2f (good to firm) in first-time blinkers; 125-1 but wasn't disgraced when fourth at Huntingdon (2m, good to soft) in this headgear combination on stable/hurdling debut at the start of last month; might build on that.

stable_tour.quote: He has improved for a step up in trip and ran into one of Sir Mark Prescott's called Deep Water Bay at Wolverhampton the other day. He's physically developed and he'll improve as the season goes on. There's lots of fun to be had for the Fellowship Racing and Diskovery syndicate. 11-06-25

runners.comment: Two bumpers and a hurdles run suggest he'll be more at home in modest handicaps.
runners.spotlight: Started life in a Listed bumper but that run and the two that followed it, including over hurdles three weeks ago, suggest he'll be more at home in modest handicaps.

runners.comment: Has been weakening but tongue-tie may help and the pair that beat him last time are useful
runners.spotlight: Won a Flat race for newcomers at Le Mans (1m3f, good to soft) in May on his only start in France; dropped out tamely to be well beaten on hurdling debut at Fontwell (2m1f, good to soft; 11-4) in November and it was a weakening third at Wincanton (1m7f, soft) in January; the pair who finished in front of him that day are decent sorts, however, and maybe the tongue-tie will help; considered.

stable_tour.quote: A winner of his only start on the Flat in France, a middle-distance maiden in the provinces, he has joined our team of juvenile hurdlers and I like him. He's pleased us in all his work and should be ready to make his debut in a juvenile hurdle around the middle of the month. 04-11-25

racecards.verdict: A race that revolves around smart Flat horse AIMERIC but the suggestion is ONE ISLAND, who may benefit from a first-time tongue-tie.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/2 Aimeric, 3/1 Miss Kingston, 4/1 One Island, 5/1 Cheap Sandwiches, 10/1 Just Call Me Buzz, 12/1 Louis Des Landes, 16/1 Nowherenearmilan, 20/1 Teletime, 33/1 Five Valleys, 50/1 Scrumpyjack,  Maestrow, 66/1 Footage Detectives

racecards.race_name: Dunraven Windows Gats And Co Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.breeder: S A S I E I & Percy Holding Aps
runners.comment: Consistent before finding a Class 2 over further too big an ask here latest; player.
runners.spotlight: Jumping let him down in what was effectively a 0-150 handicap here latest (2m3f, good to soft); his string of low-130s RPRs before that read well in tonight's company, however, and although still 9lb above any mark defied he did land a C&D novice handicap last year on one other visit.

quotes.race: Capital Windscreens Supports Autism Charity Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were utilising Torneo's weight-for-age allowance earlier on in the season. That's run out now so he didn't have the benefit of that, but he's still done it very nicely - Jamie Snowden, trainer.

quotes.race: Every Race Live On Racing TV Juvenile Hurdle (Go North Grey Bomber Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's job done. Torneo's jumping wasn't always fluent but I'll take the blame for that. We could have gone winging away but I didn't feel the need to go long at all of them. The ground is hard work. He's a fine, big horse with a lovely attitude. He's still a bit raw so hopefully there's more to come - Gavin Sheehan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He was a nice novice hurdler but he really stepped up when going novice handicap chasing, utilising his four-year-old weight-for-age allowance. He won twice and was unlucky not to win a third time when he fell at the Scottish National meeting. He finished second at Wetherby on a nice comeback run and there's plenty more to come. 05-11-25
A new arrival, he ran on the Flat in France and seems tough and talented as he never finished out of the first four in six starts. He looks a ready-made type for juvenile hurdling over here. 28-09-23

runners.comment: Struggling for form since November's hurdles second; unconvincing chase debut latest.
runners.spotlight: Chance on November's Doncaster hurdles second, less so on all which has followed; unexposed in this sphere, with one start over fences compared to the other trio's 41 combined, but none too convincing on that belated chase debut at Wetherby latest (1m7f, good), jumping left and weakening.

quotes.race: Country Food Trust Fakenham Silver Cup Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I would have fancied Paramount in the Imperial Cup but he came here instead and it was a great bit of placing by Charlie Longsdon. Like most of his family he'll improve for a fence - Aidan Coleman, jockey.

quotes.race: Sky Bet UKs No.1 Betting App Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Parramount was good. He's qualified for the EBF Final and that's the main target. We ran him in a handicap last time and he got beat because he wasn't mentally ready. That's his immaturity, so we decided to come for a novice. I'll try to run him in a handicap before the EBF because he needs to be rated 120-plus. We know he's got ability and he's got more speed than his sister (Snow Leopardess) -      Charlie Longsdon, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's an exciting prospect who we'll look to step up in level after winning well last time out. He's a big horse, very leggy, so the plan has always been to go chasing with him eventually. However, I'd like him to get more experience this season before we try that, as he hasn't raced all that much for a six-year-old. 20-11-22

This half-brother to Snow Leopardess has failed to make the first three in only one of his seven races, such is his consistency. He won at Hereford on his penultimate outing and I thought he would win last time out at Taunton on his handicap debut but he got into a slight argument with his jockey and on a sharp track like that he did not get home. He is well handicapped off his current mark of 115 and I have a lot of time for him. He is a very strong-travelling horse, and I am keen to step him up further in trip. I am sure he can win another novice hurdle with his penalty but it will only be when he goes chasing that you will see the real Parramount. 11-01-23

runners.comment: Back to within 2lb of the mark he lowered at Taunton in January (2m, good); stable debut.
runners.spotlight: Able to dominate when cashing in a career-low mark at Taunton in January (2m, good), his sole win in 14 chasing starts; hasn't gone on since, but back to within 2lb of that figure now and one previous wind operation provoked a small spike in form; chance on first start for new yard.

quotes.race: 12 February Valentines Meeting Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I was really pleased, as Hypotenus's last run was a horrible experience for him. He came back from that battered and bruised, with cuts and marks all over him, which was frustrating. He's not the type to endure a hustle or bustle; he likes to get into his own rhythm. I was wondering whether his confidence would be okay after Ludlow. He did have to lug a big weight, but I was still hoping for a big race. He ran some nice races for us last year without winning; he was beaten by Vincenzo and everything that beat him looked like a nice horse - Joe Tickle, trainer.

quotes.race: Xenon Security Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: We were hoping coming here that there would be a bit of pace for Hypotenus so that we could drop in a small bit but nobody wanted to make it so Keith kept it simple. He went a good gallop on testing ground - Gavin Cromwell, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's another newcomer to the yard and made a winning start in a maiden hurdle at Gowran at the end of September. The ground was heavy there, but he's a better horse on better ground - he has plenty of gears and travels a bit too strong in that winter ground, so two miles is far enough for him in it. He's definitely better going right-handed but we're going to give him a go at Naas for a four-year-old winners' race on Sunday. 10-11-23

runners.comment: Exeter and Chepstow winner with cut; plenty of chances off tonight's sort of mark.
runners.spotlight: Sometime tendency to jump right hasn't been sufficient to deny him victory around here in the past, and he's never hit the deck in 22 career starts; issue is more that he's now 0-10 racing from official marks above the 104 he denied at Exeter in January (2m1f, good to soft).

racecards.verdict: Back down from last time's Class 2 company and 2m3f trip, TORNEO's consistency over the winter earns him the nod over Hypotenus.
racecards.betting_forecast: Evs Torneo, 11/4 Hypotenus, 5/1 Parramount,  Bonza Boy

racecards.race_name: Sun Trade Windows Cherry Gold Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Bumped into an even less exposed handicapper over C&D latest (pair 9l clear); player.
runners.spotlight: Endured a sobering chase debut here in November (sole start on good) but firmly back on track on sole start since when finding only an even less exposed handicapper too good over C&D a fortnight ago (good to soft; pair 9l clear); cheekpieces added; retains plenty of upside.

quotes.race: Amazing Sri Lanka EBF "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (Qualifier) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The Kemble Brewery has always been a good horse. He won his two bumpers but he sliced into the back of his tendon when he ran at Cheltenham and was within millimetres of not being with us. His owners run a pub in Cheltenham and they've been very patient - Kim Bailey, trainer.

quotes.race: Cheltenham & South West Racing Club Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: The Kemble Brewery has won a decent bumper today and that's all that matters. I think we'll probably go over hurdles, but we will see how takes this race. He is very unfazed by anything, and he has already schooled and jumped well - Kim Bailey, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a very nice horse and we've always liked him. He's so laid-back it's ridiculous- if he was a human he would drive you demented because he's got so much talent and ability, but you'd want to kick him before he actually did anything. We'll definitely take a step up in grade now and his form is working out very well. He's a very talented individual with plenty of speed. 19-11-24

He's the biggest talking horse we've trained in a long time as his form had worked out so well. We didn't know whether to go hurdling or chasing but, after schooling him at the back end of last season he was brilliant, so we thought we'd let him do what he's bred for. All his work and schooling through the spring had been very good, but he got a very bad fall at Chepstow in November. He didn't have a cut at his fences like we thought he would. He's had a break since then and you'll see him back over hurdles towards the end of January. You'd hope there's an awful lot of progress to come from him. 24-12-25

runners.comment: Aintree flop latest isn't without precedent; easier task here and ought not mind a dryout.
runners.spotlight: For two years in a row now he's followed a second in the Imperial Cup with a disappointing effort at Aintree, second-time cheekpieces presumably not to blame latest as they're retained here; record of 1F12 in handicaps of Class 3 or below, and ought not mind any dryout (2-4 on good).

quotes.race: Visit Irish Bloodstock Sales With ITM Junior 'National Hunt' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was a bit of a messy race. Wreckless Eric jumped seriously well at Newbury apart from the second-last, but he's a very good jumper. They didn't really go much of a gallop and he made his own running. He made mistakes along the way and was very green up the home straight - Ben Pauling, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was a model of consistency last season and was unlucky not to get the rub of the green when second in the Imperial Cup. He ran in a lot of competitive handicaps and was on the go for a long time, so Aintree might have been one race too many. He will jump a fence, but he's still only five and there's no reason he can't progress further over hurdles first. Races like the Ladbroke, Imperial Cup and the County Hurdle are the sort of races we can look at. 18-11-25

runners.breeder: E A R L Haras Du Mondant
runners.comment: C&D novice winner this time last year; handicap win came off just 2lb lower; chance.
runners.spotlight: Never able to get competitive returning from five months out in a big-field Sussex Champion Hurdle recently, but September's handicap debut win came off only 2lb lower than today's mark and he landed a good-ground C&D novice event exactly a year ago; could well get back on track.

quotes.race: Tip Top Duel Flush Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It takes a bit of doing to win a novice under a penalty so I'm really pleased with Inside Man. I think we'll school him next week and try to go chasing with him next season - Jane Williams, trainer.

quotes.race: DragonBet Oncourse Service Online Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Inside Man can be a bit busy and needs to learn to settle, switch off and come with a run, which he did here. He's a Manatee and they tend to want soft ground. He's a chaser in the long term - Jane Williams, trainer, talking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: Making the running wouldn't have suited him at Taunton last time but he was still able to win. He's shown plenty in two starts, having only just been beaten by Liari on his debut at Wincanton. The Triumph trial at Cheltenham this month is a possibility for him. He'd learn nothing in another junior or juvenile hurdle under a penalty, whereas if he goes up in grade he will be running against proper horses and a good gallop, which would suit him. 11-01-24

runners.comment: Pestered in lead and made errors on recent return; would certainly appreciate a dryout.
runners.spotlight: Taunton win this time last year was the first leg of an eventual hat-trick (2m1f-2m3f) all recorded on good or quicker surfaces, so drying forecast is all to the good; chance, assuming he's not goaded into making the same sorts of errors as on his recent return here.

stable_tour.quote: He's been a great summer horse, winning five of his last seven races, and we'll keep him on the go. He'll stay on decent ground, and we also have the option to go chasing with him at some point. 12-11-25

A chaser for the future as he's a big, strong horse. He was a bit disappointing last time but stopped quickly. We've given him a wind operation and he's got a mark of 108, which I think would make him thrown in. He wouldn't mind a bit of decent ground, so he'll be ready to run at the end of the month and I think he's really well handicapped. He's quite a nice horse. 18-01-24

runners.comment: Leicester win and two C&D seconds since Christmas all gained with some give underfoot.
runners.spotlight: C&D seconds either side of January's Leicester win (1m7f, heavy) speak well of his effectiveness around galloping tracks with at least some give underfoot; drying forecast worries more than latest 1lb rise.

racecards.verdict: Less exposed in handicaps than dual Imperial Cup second Wreckless Eric, C&D runner-up THE KEMBLE BREWERY (nap) can go one better.
racecards.betting_forecast: 15/8 The Kemble Brewery, 2/1 Wreckless Eric, 5/1 Razzle Dazzle Boy, 6/1 Inside Man,  American Land

racecards.race_name: Dunraven Bowl Pink Eyed Pedro "Grassroots' Open Hunters" Chase

runners.comment: Proved stamina for 3m with ease at Exeter latest (good) and still on the up; big player.
runners.spotlight: Rampant in sub-3m good-ground hurdle races and chases last summer, and has the beating of Yippee Ki Yay on a line through Macklin, whom he trounced at Exeter last time (3m, good); still fairly lightly raced over this sort of trip, and drying forecast rates a big plus.

quotes.race: Pricing By Real Bookmakers At dragonbet.co.uk Novices' Hurdle (Arc Summer Novices' Brush Hdl) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Stumps Or Slips is full of confidence and has probably been running in races that haven't been competitive. He's at the right end of the handicap and it helped he was able to run in a competitive race with no penalties. He's been a real fun horse for connections, but things are going to get tougher now. He hasn't improved, but he's been refreshed with a new set of surroundings, which he's enjoying. Tom [Weston] has been really helpful and it was nice of him to suggest the change of scenery. He'll go to the final of this series now, so he won't run until the middle of September - Olly Murphy.

runners.comment: Won this in 2025, six years after first taking the same prize; 2l second on recent return.
runners.spotlight: Splendid old-timer who has won both confined novice (2019) and grassroots (2025) incarnations of this race (each on good); always held by a match-fit and five-years younger rival on this month's seasonal return, albeit beaten just 2l; likely to be spot on for his title defence.

quotes.race: John Ayres Memorial Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We'll look for another race for Pink Eyed Pedro. He seems to like Chepstow and this is his ground - David Brace, trainer.

prev_owners.owner: Giddy Up Ideal Du Tabert Syndicate

runners.comment: This season's form is a bit better than it first appears; not dismissed out of hand.
runners.spotlight: Successive 2025 point wins (3m, good to soft) were each gained in the day's fastest time; this season's form is a bit better than it first appears, considering some hikes in class and mostly tougher underfoot conditions, and he's not dismissed out of hand.

runners.comment: Late-2024 defeat of Barton Snow looks better form now; unseated at Stratford last Sunday.
runners.spotlight: Remains the last horse to beat hunter chase star Barton Snow, albeit back in late 2024 on desperate ground; twice a Trebudannon open point winner (good to soft) since January's Hereford hunter chase exit which was not of his own making, but an unseat at Stratford last Sunday is harder to forgive.

runners.comment: Hampered when unseating latest; experienced chaser, with all wins on softer than good.
runners.spotlight: Hampered when unseating in an open point at neighbouring Howick last month, and generally a safe ride; both handicap chase wins (from 17 starts over fences) have come over Wincanton's 3m1f on ground softer than good, and the drying forecast isn't strictly ideal.

quotes.race: Play Tote Cheltenham Ten To Follow Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Poppa Poutine is only six, amazingly. He'll be a good stayer for years to come and goes on a lot worse ground. He'll be the type for those regional Nationals. He's a great ride and is honest. He'll take you wherever you want to be, but he's a bit idle when he gets there. At the same time, he's a grand horse - Sam Twiston-Davies, jockey.

runners.comment: Blameless exit behind Stumps Or Slips latest, but not in the form this year to figure.
runners.spotlight: Landed back-to-back Fontwell and Wincanton staying handicap chases three years ago (good to soft); blameless exit behind Stumps Or Slips latest (hampered) but capable of throwing in his own errors or jumping right; form of this year's completed efforts falls well short of the required.

quotes.race: GBIM Women Investors Network Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: I was worried when the fizz seemed to go out of Windance with a circuit to go, but he's obviously got a gear he can keep going at. Every time a fence came, he gained a length and it was a great ride. Hopefully he can go on and keep creeping away. I didn't think we'd be running because the ground looked set to be quick and he has had a tendon, which is why he's had a big gap in his career - Anthony Honeyball, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's won his last two chases and jumps great. He looks to handle most ground and I think he'll still be competitive off his current mark. There should be more to come and he's a straightforward horse. 12-10-23

runners.owner: Mr And Mrs Ben Herbert And Family

prev_owners.owner: And Mrs Ben Herbert And Family
Mr And Mrs Ben Herbert And Family
Mr And Mrs Ben Herbert And Family
Mr And Mrs Ben Herbert And Family
Mr And Mrs Ben Herbert And Family

runners.comment: Appears to have something to find with Stumps Or Slips, but no track or going type issues.
runners.spotlight: Track and going types come alike to this former Kelso and Exeter hunter chase winner (soft and good to soft); 11l behind a rival later drubbed by Stumps Or Slips on his most recent hunter chase start, but confidence levels topped up with an easy point win at Eyton-on-Severn (good to firm) since.

stable_tour.quote: He won two hunter chases last season at Exeter and Kelso. He'll probably have some hunter chase engagements again, although whether he'll be up to top-class hunter chases with penalties and whatever is a bit doubtful. But he certainly improved from his first to his second season with us and I can see him improving again. He seems much more mature now and it was a terrific win at Kelso in May. 28-11-24

racecards.verdict: Still fairly lightly raced at this sort of trip, STUMPS OR SLIPS is taken to deny veteran Pink Eyed Pedro a third Dunraven Bowl.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/8 Stumps Or Slips, 11/4 Pink Eyed Pedro, 4/1 Yippee Ki Yay, 15/2 Important Notice, 14/1 Ideal Du Tabert, 16/1 Poppa Poutine, 33/1 Windance

racecards.race_name: Braceys Master Charm Mares' Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Stopped early latest, but broke course record for Kempton's 3m over Christmas (good).
runners.spotlight: Effectively a 0-135 mares' handicap she took in course record time at Kempton over Christmas (good); can throw in the odd poor effort and there's something to take on trust after she stopped early on latest start (made a noise) but she's in the mix if all is well with her.

stable_tour.quote: Another very smart mare. We were delighted to get her as we didn't think we'd be able to afford her at the sales in December. She won first time out at Fakenham in April, despite getting knocked sideways and the track being too sharp for her. She doesn't show much at home and you'll only see how good she is in the last half-mile of a race. She probably wouldn't have the size and scope of Metkayina or Jasmine Bliss, but she's a warrior. She'll start out next month and we don't know how good she can be, so the dream is alive. 24-10-24

runners.comment: Mixed signals this term as to her present optimum trip, but weighted to strike again.
runners.spotlight: Sole 3m success was gained off tonight's mark in autumn 2022 (good); just one further win since (2m5f) and mixed signals this term as to her present optimum trip, but unarguably weighted to strike again.

stable_tour.quote: She's progressing and should pick up another little race. If it's a case of running her with a double penalty, I can take 7lb off her with Kai Lenihan on top. 21-11-22

runners.comment: Well named from a handicapping perspective, upped 13lb since December without winning.
runners.spotlight: Worcester novice scorer (2m4f, good) last May having gone close here previously; no further win but still upped 13lb since December, finding Kilworth almost 4l too good at Ascot (3m, good) on penultimate start; appears vulnerable to that mare and other rivals again here, as shown once more when fourth at Warwick on Thursday.

stable_tour.quote: She was second at Aintree on Boxing Day, but last time she got stuck at Ludlow when finishing seventh. I think we can forget that run. She's run well before. You'll notice the handicapper hasn't moved her mark from 108 since being well beaten at Ludlow, but there we are. We'll probably try to find better ground. It's very hard to find races for this type of horse. There are lots of really bad races for the 0-100s but there are very few 0-110s or 0-120s because the racecourses don't want to put them on as they cost too much money. Unfortunately, we're catering for mediocrity nowadays. 18-02-26

runners.comment: Taunton and Ascot winner either side of a possibly forgivable Plumpton blip; up 7lb.
runners.spotlight: Her worst performance in Irish points had been recorded on soft, so perhaps February's Plumpton failure on similar ground ought not to have surprised; nicely progressive in staying handicaps otherwise with wins at Taunton and Ascot, though the 7lb rise since the latter asks a stiff question.

stable_tour.quote: She won a point-to-point in Ireland and was a staying-on fifth in a bumper. She's an absolute sweetheart. All she wants to do is please you and her work is lovely. She's going to be a stayer. 05-11-25

runners.comment: Close second at Ffos Las (3m, heavy) was not built upon when back up to this class latest.
runners.spotlight: Just one win in 24, and Ffos Las near-miss on second outing for current handler likely owed something to the drop to 0-105 company (3m, heavy); limitations exposed again since and this is tougher still.

runners.comment: Below par on two of her last three outings, including latest; trip is not an obvious plus.
runners.spotlight: Below par on two of her last three outings, including latest when returned to the sound surface of her one career success; hasn't shaped as if in need of this second crack at a stayers' trip (pulled up in the first).

quotes.race: Rhino.Bet Proudly Sponsor Henry Brooke Mares' Maiden Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Roaring Home is a nice filly. Henry (Daly, trainer) did say to me she'll just lack a bit of fitness and she had a good blow turning in, so I switched her in to try and save a bit and have one go at the horse in front. I was surprised how well she picked up and she's got an awful lot of improvement to come - Harry Cobden, jockey, talking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Seemed to pass stamina test over this C&D latest; up from 0-115 company but respected.
runners.spotlight: Big-field Navan winner in autumn 2024 and best British efforts have similarly been recorded in handicap hurdles around galloping tracks; trip didn't beat her when upped to this C&D latest (good to soft), failing by just over 2l, and she's not wholly dismissed despite the hotter company.

racecards.verdict: If she can prove 3m is her present optimum, I SPY A DIVA is weighted to strike at the expense of Kilworth and Star Walking.
racecards.betting_forecast: 2/1 Star Walking, 11/4 Kilworth, 4/1 Hard Dealt, 6/1 I Spy A Diva, 9/1 Love Me, 12/1 Roaring Home, 16/1 Slim Marvel

racecards.race_name: Grace And Dotty Handicap

runners.comment: Should come on for her reappearance and on a fair mark on her 2025 best; respected
runners.spotlight: Three 5f wins on turf last summer; on a competitive mark and she should come on for her recent return to action at Pontefract; seems to handle most ground; one to consider.

runners.comment: 5f Catterick win 16 days ago but ran poorly at Thirsk on Saturday (6f); others stronger
runners.spotlight: Ran poorly at Thirsk on Saturday (6f) but he had earlier won a 5f handicap at Catterick in determined fashion; others appeal more.

quotes.race: goracing.co.uk Future Stars Apprentice Classified Stakes
quotes.quote: Golden Prosperity is limited but that's four races he's won. He's worth more than a racehorse as he leads the two-year-olds at home every spring. I ride him every morning so he must be a quiet ride! - Tony Coyle, joint-trainer.

runners.comment: Conditions no problem and arrives on the back of an AW win; each-way claims once more
runners.spotlight: Produced late when winning a 5f handicap at Southwell three weeks ago; has the ability to defy a 3lb rise and she has run well over C&D in the past; one for the shortlist.

quotes.race: Rob Burrow Dare To Dream Handicap
quotes.quote: Opal Storm likes the place but she just needs a bit of luck in running - Brian Rothwell, trainer.

runners.comment: Ended 2025 in good order; still feasibly weighted & he's one to consider back from a break
runners.spotlight: Off the mark at the 14th attempt when landing a 5f handicap at Beverley last September (soft) and ran well for fourth of 14 at Musselburgh one month later (good Topspeed figure); could progress further this year and he has shown promise on good to firm.

runners.breeder: Mr & Mrs S Matheson & Mr S Goodwin
runners.comment: 6f win here last May off 2lb higher; promise two starts ago but couldn't back it up latest
runners.spotlight: Progressive last spring, following a 5f AW win with a ready 6f win at this track (good to firm); mixed bag since then but his penultimate fourth at Wolverhampton was encouraging; failed to back it up ten days later but no doubt the ability is there and he's well handicapped now.

stable_tour.quote: He's been a bit frustrating as he's not always cooperative going into the stalls. He also pulls hard given too much daylight and needs the race run to suit. He's a handy horse though and he'll run over five furlongs next time. 08-04-26

runners.comment: Three solid runs on AW since fitted with a visor; more to prove on turf but not ruled out
runners.spotlight: Ready win in a first-time visor at Newcastle last month (5f); perfectly good efforts in defeat twice since, coming from well back having blown the start at Newcastle on Monday (6f); more to prove on turf but this should be run to suit.

runners.comment: Ended 2025 with two good runs but well short of that level so far in 2026; risky
runners.spotlight: Ended 2025 with two placed efforts on AW and he lines up here off a 6lb lower mark than when second at Newcastle in December; that is a result of four lesser efforts though and he now has a point to prove.

runners.breeder: Julia Scott, J F Dean, M L W Bell
runners.comment: On handy mark and latest Pontefract fourth can be upgraded (wide on home turn); e-w shout
runners.spotlight: Ended a losing run when the comfortable winner of a 5f handicap at Nottingham last May (5f, good to firm) off a 1lb higher mark; he was returning from a short break when fourth of 13 at Pontefract 17 days ago and that effort can be upgraded as he was wider than ideal as the field turned for home; each-way shout.

quotes.race: At The Races App Form Study "Confined" Apprentice Handicap (For horses Which Have Not Won In 2023)
quotes.quote: The plan was to take a lead on Masterclass and he picked up nicely when I asked him. He liked the ground and has a good attitude - Brandon Wilkie, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He won well at Nottingham then ran another solid race at Redcar, where he was unlucky and got struck into behind. He has run well since but disappointed last week at Nottingham as he had a perfect pitch and at the furlong-marker I thought he was going to win but he didn't pick up, for whatever reason. 14-08-25

runners.comment: Conditions fine and on a dangerous mark so he can't be discounted despite his absence
runners.spotlight: Veteran with a better record on AW than turf; 5f on fast ground no problem for him and he has run well after an absence in the past (although not last year); good run wouldn't be a surprise but others appeal more for win purposes.

quotes.race: Read Katie Walsh On Betway Insider Handicap
quotes.quote: Newyorkstateofmind picked up for me in the straight, he's very honest and genuine. The gap opened up for us. He's been in great form lately - Ray Dawson.

stable_tour.quote: Three wins from 13 races last year was a nice return for this fellow, two on the all-weather and one on grass. Six of his nine wins have been on the all-weather and when it comes to the turf, he has to have theound fast. He was a bit disappointing when he returned to Wolverhampton from his winter break, but it is onwards and upwards. There's a race at Thirsk on Saturday that looks right for him. 09-04-25

runners.comment: Just one win from 17 starts but she arrives on the back of a good third at Catterick
runners.spotlight: Won a 5f classified event at Redcar last summer; close third to Golden Prosperity at Catterick 16 days ago (5f, good), always prominent; needs a bit more if she's to come out on top in this competitive sprint.

runners.comment: 12-race maiden but capable and he's tumbled down weights; dangerous if the new hood works
runners.spotlight: 0-12 and well beaten at Newcastle when last seen in November; he was sent off favourite on that occasion and returns from a break off a 2lb lower mark; no doubt the ability is there to win races if the addition of a hood has a calming effect (often races too freely).

runners.comment: Strongly run 5f suits her best; went close on AW last month; each-way shout
runners.spotlight: Losing run stands at 17 but she has run some good races in defeat for Joey Ramsden and a strongly run race at this trip should see her to best effect; unraced on faster than good; each-way shout if the ground is no issue.

runners.comment: Exposed 20-race maiden but often placed and a recent run should have sharpened him up
runners.spotlight: Still seeking his first win after 20 attempts but there have been several good runs along the way; recent return from a ten-month layoff should have sharpened him up and he holds each-way claims.

stable_tour.quote: He ran really well last week at Brighton when he was unlucky not to win. The first-time blinkers helped him in the first part of the race more than anything as he wasn't getting into gear in enough time. He's well handicapped off his mark of 54 as he's a 65-rated horse on his day. He's been second on three of his last four starts and is unlucky not to have won by now, but he'll have his day. Five furlongs is too short for him and going up to 6f on a galloping track will suit him better. He may head to Carlisle on Friday and he'll be winning pretty soon. 30-05-24

runners.comment: Promising 4th on stable debut last month (6f, AW); a bigger effort could be brewing
runners.spotlight: Tried over as far as 1m4f when trained by Martin Dunne; won a 7f event in Jersey last June; absent for 276 days prior to a close fourth at Wolverhampton last month (6f; first time in these retained accessories), an effort that can be marked up as she made a big move in the middle section of the race while racing on the outside of the field; dropping to 5f is new but a strongly run race at the trip could suit; suspicion a bigger effort is brewing.

runners.comment: 17-race maiden with just one handicap run that makes her of interest; absent 139 days
runners.spotlight: 0-17 and just one handicap run that makes her of interest, namely her close third at Ripon last July; absent for 139 days and others have more pressing claims.

runners.comment: Not much to shout about in the last 18 months and easy enough to swerve
runners.spotlight: Good runs have been few and far between since his Wolverhampton second in September 2024; easy enough to swerve.

runners.comment: Five-time winner but out of sorts so far this year; not a solid option
runners.spotlight: Five-time winner but he has been short of his best on AW this year and the return to turf made no difference at Bath 19 days ago; not a solid option.

racecards.verdict: Wide open but Masterclass and NO GAIN look interesting contenders, both having run better than their position suggests last time.

racecards.race_name: Summer Saturday Series Handicap

runners.comment: Three turf wins; never dangerous on AW return in February but might do better this time
runners.spotlight: Can miss the break but scored twice last year, a 20-1 win at Newmarket (good to firm) in July supplemented by a Yarmouth (also 7f, good to soft) success in September; never dangerous on AW return in February but might do better this time.

runners.comment: Rusty on turf return a fortnight ago; candidate to build on that; first-time tongue-tie
runners.spotlight: In decent nick on AW for this yard since August, in the frame all seven starts and scoring at Newcastle (1m) in October; looked rusty on his turf reappearance a fortnight ago but he's a candidate to build on that; first-time tongue-tie.

runners.comment: 0-9 for this yard; career-low mark and second go at this trip the straws to clutch at
runners.spotlight: Got up late to win Bath novice (5f, good to firm) for Andrew Balding in June; 0-9 for this yard (majority 6f, turf/AW) and first-time cheekpieces (removed) didn't spark an improved effort last time; career-low mark and second go at this trip (first is easily excused) the straws to clutch at.

quotes.race: Swindon Designer Outlet British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It's a good job Pianoforte stays six [furlongs] on this slightly slower ground now they've got a bit of rain into it. They've gone fast and it was nice he had something to aim at for a long time. He's tightened up from Catterick and come on today and I think there's plenty more to come - Callum Hutchinson, jockey.

runners.comment: Market support before a winning stable debut; up 7lb for this reappearance
runners.spotlight: Attracted market interest on first go for John Berry and it was rewarded with a win at Yarmouth (7f, good to firm) in August; up 7lb and absent since so interesting to see how she goes in the market this time.

stable_tour.quote: She's been a bit of an enigma. I think she's got a fair bit of ability and has been placed a fair few times but we're just struggling to find the key to getting her nose in front. She's had trouble in running and a few different things just not going right. She ran at Ayr on Monday, finishing third behind Spun To Gold. 17-07-25

runners.breeder: M H Sly & Mrs P M Sly
runners.owner: G Libson And Mrs P Sly
runners.comment: Won three of his last four including AW return; has to be of interest under a 3lb nudge
runners.spotlight: Won three of his last four, comprising two wins at Leicester (good to soft) and an AW success at Southwell (also 7f) on this month's comeback; big field no bother and he has to be of interest under a 3lb nudge.

quotes.race: Visit racingtv.com Apprentice Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: I'm pleased Wrydcroft ran well because I always thought he was okay. We've had difficulty getting him handicapped, and I had to run him over a mile on his last start, which I knew was too far, but you have to do it. It's a jump to find three-year-old maidens unless I want to go to Hamilton or Ffos Las, and that's an awfully long way for us to go to just have one in a maiden. He's been a bit of a slow learner but Kieran O'Neill, who has ridden him, said he'll be a really nice horse. I knew he wanted a bit of give in the ground because all those bred out of Speciosa want that. Hopefully, he'll go up four or five pounds and he should be somewhere in the mid-60s once he gets himself organised - Pam Sly, trainer.

runners.comment: Has ability but inconsistent; watch the market on reappearance/stable debut
runners.spotlight: 0-8 for Roger Varian but displayed clear ability on AW (tailed off on sole turf start) while also lacking consistency; sold for 5,000gns in December and wind surgery swiftly followed; market might help on this reappearance/stable debut.

runners.breeder: Al Shaqab Racing & S C E A Des Prairies
runners.comment: No immediate encouragement on stable debut a fortnight ago

runners.spotlight: Improved for the switch to handicaps when winning at Newcastle (7f) in September and bettered that form when third over 6f at Southwell (also AW) in November; had wind surgery before respectable comeback over latter C&D one month ago; unexposed on turf and worth a second look.

She's likely to go to Doncaster on Friday for one of the new races that have been put on there. I'm hoping that if all goes well she can go up in grade after that. stable_tour.quote: She ran well at Thirsk last time when she was third behind Ryka, earning her an opening mark of 71. The plan is to run her in a 7f nursery next, possibly at Carlisle on Thursday. 28-08-24

runners.comment: C&D winner; step back in the right direction latest; considered
runners.spotlight: Made virtually all in big-field York handicap (good to firm) in 2024; C&D (good to soft; first-time tongue-tie) and AW (also 7f) winner last summer; lesser efforts followed until a firm step back in the right direction last time and returns to turf from a handy mark; respected.

runners.comment: Ran well latest (AW); rare foray on grass but not dismissed from his lower turf mark

quotes.race: Unibet More Extra Place Races Handicap
quotes.quote: I think the gelding (operation) has helped and a bit of a break and Giant has come back fresh and well. Everything went to plan and he's done it nicely - Richard Spencer, trainer, speaking on Racing TV.

runners.comment: Running well with races spaced out; player if this doesn't come too soon
runners.spotlight: 0-16 on turf but he went mighty close at Redcar (good) in October; narrow winner at Southwell (also 7f, AW) on next start in December and it was a good effort when third to Wrydcroft over latter C&D last time; that did come after another two-month break but he's a player if backing it up 17 days on.

runners.comment: 0-16 (includes turf); had this headgear combination when fourth (AW) latest
runners.spotlight: 0-16 (includes turf) but has gone close a couple of times on AW; wore this headgear combination when fourth at Wolverhampton (8.5f, AW) under Hope Regan three weeks ago.

runners.comment: Close third (7f, good) on return to turf a fortnight ago; chance off same mark
runners.spotlight: Won at Newcastle (AW) in September and it was a close third at Thirsk (also 7f, good) on his return to turf a fortnight ago; drawn on the wing but can travel smoothly and should be in the thick of it off the same mark.

runners.comment: Won division of this in 2024; mark fine; possibilities
runners.spotlight: Good record here with three wins including a division of this (soft; acts on good/good to firm) in 2024; cashed in on reduced mark to open AW account over 7f in November and just 1lb higher on this return to turf after three months away; possibilities.

quotes.race: Thank You To Doncaster Annual Members Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: Onemorenomore is a jockey's dream, he's very straightforward - just switch him off early and try not to get there too soon - Billy Loughnane, jockey.

But he did exactly the same thing here last year, just getting there on the nod in the last 20 yards. He's that type of horse, we ride him behind at home and he always finishes off his gallops. runners.comment: Minor promise in two AW runs (1m/7f) this spring; handicaps will provide better openings
runners.spotlight: Signs of ability in two runs at Newcastle this spring (1m/7f); likely to find life easier once handicapping.

runners.comment: Well backed when third in a Newbury maiden (6.5f, soft) last October; open to improvement
runners.spotlight: Finished third of eight, beaten 3l, when the well-backed favourite for a 6.5f maiden at Newbury last October (soft; winner has since finished fourth in the Greenham); could see his race out more strongly on the sounder surface; big player.

stable_tour.quote: He ran a decent race on his debut and is working well at the moment. He looks like one to follow. 21-04-26

runners.comment: 45,000gns yearling; sold unraced for 1,000gns last October; likely best watched on debut
runners.spotlight: Fetched 55,000gns as a foal and 45,000gns as a yearling but went through the ring for just 1,000gns last October; second foal; half-brother to Canadian 7f AW winner Vrana; dam French Listed-placed 6.5f 2yo winner (RPR 90); likely best watched on debut.

runners.comment: Useful ability but can over-race and isn't progressing; still a key player in this field
runners.spotlight: Free-going sort; has shown a fair level of ability in his four starts and has the strongest form on offer; could do with settling better though and appears vulnerable to anything progressive.

runners.owner: Sheikh Hamdan bin Mohammed Al Maktoum
runners.comment: 240,000gns yearling; dam a useful and well-related winner; can play a part on debut
runners.spotlight: 240,000gns yearling; second foal of an 8.6f/1m3f winner (including US; RPR 98), herself a half-sister to winners Gifts Of Gold (smart 1m1f-1m7f) and Dusky Queen (7f Listed); appealing pedigree and no surprise to see him play a part on debut.

runners.comment: Top-class pedigree; represents a powerful stable and is of obvious interest on paper
runners.spotlight: Top-class pedigree, closely related to three winners, notably Group 1 winner Benbatl (RPR 124) and a half-brother to three other winners including 1000 Guineas heroine Elmalka (113); dam a Grade/Group 1 winner over 1m2f (118); five of those six winning siblings were successful first time out; of obvious interest.

racecards.verdict: Bunyola Bay can leave his 2yo debut behind him but the eye is drawn to MOREEDD's sparkling pedigree.
racecards.betting_forecast: 5/4 Moreedd, 3/1 Bunyola Bay,  Deported, 5/1 Glen Nevis, 33/1 Balmoral Boy, 50/1 Celtic Chariot

racecards.race_name: Free Bets On attheraces.com Handicap

runners.comment: 3-5 since handicapping and he bolted up at Bath last week; faster ground today; contender
runners.spotlight: He made an instant impact once handicapping in a visor, winning over 8.6f at Wolverhampton in February and following up over 1m at Newcastle 11 days later; back on the up with an emphatic front-running success at Bath last week (1m, good to soft) and he is 2lb well in under a 6lb penalty; faster ground to contend with today but this will be his last chance in a Class 5 for a while and he has to be high on the list.

runners.comment: Six-race maiden but he's run well in all three handicaps and the drop to 1m may help
runners.spotlight: Seeking his first win but he has run well in defeat in all three handicap starts (9.4f-1m3f); drops back to 1m today and he could still have a bit more to offer.

runners.comment: Promise twice on AW last year; bred to be useful; check betting on handicap/seasonal debut
runners.spotlight: Two third-place finishes last season, both over 7f on AW; bred to be useful and market support would look significant on this seasonal and handicap debut.

runners.comment: Good second on his seasonal return this month; perhaps vulnerable to less-exposed sorts
runners.spotlight: Stepped up on his 2yo efforts when finishing second to a handicap blot at Southwell three weeks ago (1m); should give his running but perhaps vulnerable to less-exposed sorts.

runners.comment: Strong at the finish in a 1m AW novice last month; more to come in handicaps; yard in form
runners.spotlight: Well on top at the finish of a 1m novice at Southwell on his seasonal return five weeks ago; that was his first attempt at the trip and he moves into handicaps with potential and his stable going well.

runners.comment: Of interest on his turf debut last summer; 1m should suit now handicapping; shortlisted
runners.spotlight: Promising debut at Chester last July (7f, good; form worked out); no progress in two 7f runs at Newcastle afterwards but he has been gelded prior to his handicap/seasonal debut and stepping up to 1m should suit; one to be interested in.

runners.comment: Yet to fire for this yard and he looked a hard ride last time; risky on the back of that
runners.spotlight: Free-going sort; not matched 2yo form (for Harry Eustace) in three runs for new connections and he looked a hard ride at Wolverhampton last month, hanging badly right throughout; risky on the back of that.

racecards.verdict: An interesting race in which WELBURY (nap), a comfortable AW winner last month, can make it 2-2 for the year on his handicap debut.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/4 Silver State, 3/1 Toastmaster,  Welbury, 9/1 Saxophonist, 10/1 Booziebrunch,  Tarmonbarry Kid, 33/1 Attention Seeker

runners.comment: Progressive in 2025 until a low-key run in September; trainer runs two here; market useful
runners.spotlight: Progressive as a 3yo, winning at Lingfield (1m2f, good to firm) and Leicester (1m4f, good); below par on her final start in 2025 but she reportedly boiled over in the preliminaries; still has low mileage; market useful with the stable also running Myrrh.

runners.comment: Three AW wins since October (9.4f-1m4f); untried on faster than good; often slowly away
runners.spotlight: Often slowly away but it hasn't prevented her from winning three times on the AW since October (9.4f-1m4f); this trip more suitable than the 1m she tackled at Bath 19 days ago; untried on faster than good.

runners.comment: Two 1m2f Nottingham wins last July; fair mark if ready to roll after six months off
runners.spotlight: Won twice at Nottingham last July (1m2f, good and good to soft); just 1lb higher than for the second of those victories but she ended 2025 with a poor run and may not want the ground too lively.

runners.owner: Mrs C Fruhbeck and Denford Stud
runners.comment: Two good runs at Kempton in February; 1m2f should suit well; interesting now handicapping
runners.spotlight: Two improved efforts this year, runner-up at Kempton (1m) in February before making all in a 7f novice back at Kempton two weeks later; bred to stay this longer trip well and her best days could still be ahead of her.

runners.comment: Consistent rather than progressive for J Fanshawe; sold 18,000gns since latest; vulnerable
runners.spotlight: 1m AW win as a 2yo; consistent last year without looking ahead of her mark; sold out of James Fanshawe's stable for 18,000gns in October; she will need to be at the top of her game to make a winning stable debut after 193 days off.

runners.comment: Plugged on for sixth in a 1m handicap at Thirsk two weeks ago; unexposed; 1m2f should suit
runners.spotlight: Fitted with headgear for the first time at Thirsk two weeks ago (1m, good; turf debut) and ran her best race so far, keeping on for a never-dangerous sixth of 13 (beaten 3.75l); should stay this trip and she is open to further progress.

runners.comment: Improved with each run as a 2yo; steps up in trip for handicap debut; stable run two here
runners.spotlight: Improved her RPR with each of her three 2yo runs, winning at Hamilton in September (8.3f, soft; second past the post) and running well for third at Kempton one month later (1m; penalised); some encouragement for 1m2f on pedigree; stable also run Percy's Daydream.

runners.comment: Promising at up to 1m as a 2yo; midfield on return 12 days ago; now steps up in trip
runners.spotlight: In the frame in her four 2yo runs (7f-1m); only midfield on her seasonal debut 12 days ago but stepping up in trip could spark something extraa.

runners.comment: Still looked green when winning a 1m maiden in October; more to come in handicaps in 2026
runners.spotlight: Had subsequent winners back in second and third when scoring at Leicester in October (1m, good to soft), her second start; still looked to be learning her job there and she is open to further progress this year; 1m2f seems likely to suit her well; strong contender.

racecards.verdict: The two runners with the greatest potential appear to be Oh Yes You Do and ABLON. The selection can progress again upped to 1m2f.

runners.spotlight: Half-brother to a Group 3 winner; justified market support when overcoming inexperience to win a 6f maiden at Lingfield (AW) in January; open to improvement and he can make a bold bid despite his 7lb penalty; withdrawn after playing up in the preliminaries at Newcastle last month.

runners.comment: 200,000euros yearling but sold unraced for 8,000gns last October; best watched today
runners.spotlight: 200,000euros yearling; sold unraced for 8,000gns last October; first foal of a modest maiden from the family of Rock Of Gibraltar; likely best watched.

runners.breeder: Ballybin Stud Ltd & Mrs Wendy Daly
runners.comment: Third of eight in a 6f maiden at Pontefract last August; can do better but he needs to
runners.spotlight: Absent and gelded since finishing third of eight in a Pontefract maiden (6f; good to firm) 261 days ago; open to improvement but it will be required.

runners.comment: Low-level form in two slow-ground maidens last autumn; faster ground not enough to tempt
runners.spotlight: Modest form in two maidens (6.5f and 6f) on slow ground last autumn; today's faster ground needs to spark a transformation.

runners.comment: Pulled hard and finished out the back in a 7f AW maiden last month; no appeal
runners.spotlight: Pulled hard, despite wearing a hood, and was always in rear in Newcastle maiden (7f, AW; 125-1) last month; withdrawn after playing up in the stalls at Pontefract this month; can't recommend.

runners.owner: Mrs Polly Gibson & Miss Pollyanne Gibson

runners.spotlight: Couldn't land a blow in a 5f novice (good to firm; weak 15-2 chance) at last season's Dante meeting; absent for 345 days, during which time he has been gelded; has a fine sprinting pedigree so a big step forward would come as no great surprise.

runners.comment: £55,000 breeze-up 2yo; good sprinting pedigree; worth a market check
runners.spotlight: 9,000euros foal, £55,000 breeze-up 2yo; half-brother to 5f winner Ninety Nine (RPR 70); dam a Group-placed 5f/6f 2yo winner (96), out of 5f/6f winning half-sister to Group 3 winners Silca's Gift (7f) and Violette (6f); two of the trainer's four runners this year (all in the last eight days) have been successful; worth a market check.

runners.comment: 33-1, green and well beaten in a 6f novice last June; been gelded; longer-term prospect
runners.spotlight: 33-1, green and always in rear on his Redcar debut last June (6f, good to firm); gelded since; likely one for the longer term.

runners.comment: Minor promise in 2 AW runs, the latest this month; good pedigree but improvement essential
runners.spotlight: Just minor promise in two AW starts 137 days apart, the latest at Kempton (6f) 18 days ago; pedigree offers hope he will do better at some stage but such progress may come when handicapping.

runners.comment: Pleasing 2nd to rival who has boosted the form since in 6f AW maiden last month; e-w shout
runners.spotlight: He made a pleasing debut, as predicted by the betting, when second of nine at Wolverhampton last month (6f); couldn't cope with the easy winner on that occasion but that rival has since gone on to win a Newmarket handicap off a BHA mark of 85; open to improvement; each-way shout.

runners.comment: 700,000gns yearling; first foal of a Listed winner from a good family; market to guide
runners.spotlight: 700,000gns yearling; first foal of a 7f 2yo/1m4f winner (including Listed; RPR 107), herself a sister to 1m4f Listed winner Rainbow Sky; there is also some speed in the bottom line of his pedigree but, even so, longer trips should suit better in time; still warrants a close market check on debut.

runners.comment: 45,000gns yearling with three winning siblings; dam a Listed winner; market check advised
runners.spotlight: 44,000euros foal, 45,000gns yearling; sixth foal; closely related to 6f winner Pure Artistry (RPR 62), half-sister to winners Epic Pass (7.5f-1m2f including AW/Germany; 81) and Upepo (1m4f/1m5f AW; 77); dam 5f-1m winner (including Listed; 105); enough paper appeal to mean he can't be discounted.

runners.comment: Modest form in two 6f runs 323 days apart; minor handicaps beckon
runners.spotlight: Modest form in two 6f runs 323 days apart; minor handicaps beckon.

runners.comment: Dam a Group 3 winner as a 2yo; starts out at a realistic level; betting to guide
runners.spotlight: Second foal of a 5f 2yo winner (including Group 3; RPR 100); starts out in a winnable race and she needs a look in the market.

racecards.verdict: Wintercast is a newcomer of some note but BUCKLOW HILL looked promising on debut and can maintain his unbeaten record.

runners.spotlight: Steady progression in four starts for Kevin Philippart De Foy and left that yard for £26,000gns after finishing second in Nottingham nursery (about 1m, good) in October; new trip a positive on pedigree and market should help on this reappearance and stable debut.

runners.comment: Best effort when 3rd (1m2f, AW) last time; turf no problem on pedigree; h'cap debut
runners.spotlight: Narrowly recorded his best effort when staying on for third on return at Chelmsford (1m2f, AW) last month; brings potential to this handicap debut with turf no problem on pedigree.

runners.comment: Steady improver last term; pedigree says this trip helps on h'cap debut/return; gelded
runners.spotlight: Steady improvement in three qualifying runs around 1m (good/AW) last year; pedigree a pointer to him doing better over this longer trip on handicap debut/reappearance; has been gelded.

runners.comment: Close second in 1m nursery (good) in November; pedigree says this trip is the go; gelded
runners.spotlight: Tapped back into his initial promise when close second of five in Redcar nursery (1m, good) in November; gelded ahead of this comeback and he's another whose pedigree suggests this trip can unlock more.

runners.comment: Improved 2nd on AW last time; may build on that up in trip for turf and handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Showed improvement when second at Southwell (1m, AW) in March; interesting to see if he can build on that up in trip for this turf and handicap debut.

runners.owner: Berkshire Parts & Panels Ltd No1 Fanclub
runners.comment: Won 9.5f AW h'cap in February; others arguably have more scope for improvement
runners.spotlight: Two turf starts last year; made the breakthrough in his second handicap when scoring at Wolverhampton (9.5f, AW) in February; yet to build on that, however, and others arguably have more scope for improvement on this switch back to grass.

runners.owner: Dr Jamal Ahmadzadeh & Mrs D Swinburn
runners.comment: Big chunk of improvement latest; one of many who's interesting up in trip on h'cap debut
runners.spotlight: Big chunk of improvement when fourth at Southwell (1m, AW) in January; switches back to turf (sole run easily forgiven) and he's interesting up in trip on this handicap debut.

runners.comment: Best effort when fourth (1m, AW) latest; up in trip for turf/handicap debut
runners.spotlight: 200-1 but it was his best effort when fourth at Kempton (1m, AW) at the start of this month; mixed messages on pedigree for this trip but he can't be ruled out on turf/handicap debut.

runners.comment: 80-1 for her handicap debut and beaten 18l at Wolverhampton (9.5f, AW) last month
runners.spotlight: 80-1 for her handicap debut and was beaten 18l at Wolverhampton (9.5f, AW) last month; others have more compelling cases.

runners.comment: Fairly solid efforts in three AW handicaps last month; others more likely to improve
runners.spotlight: Fairly solid efforts in three AW handicaps last month but others have more scope for improvement on this switch back to turf.

stable_tour.quote: He was too big and weak as a two-year-old, but he had his three runs to get handicapped. He's come back showing a decent level of form. The owners want to win on the Flat and he's set to go to Doncaster on April 21 for his first run over a mile and a half and on grass. I think he's crying out for a trip and hurdles. 08-04-26

racecards.verdict: Very few of these mostly unexposed 3yos can be ruled out but the vote goes to KISS FOR AN ANGEL, who can improve again up in trip.
