racecards.race_name: GS Group Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Runner-up in an Irish point but it's been modest stuff under rules; readily opposed
runners.spotlight: Runner-up in an Irish point but it's been modest stuff under rules; readily opposed.

runners.breeder: Earl Haras Du Luy & Andre Duboe
runners.comment: Shaped with promise in all three bumpers but rejected by stable jockey
runners.spotlight: Shaped with promise in all three bumpers (soft/good) but Sean Bowen rides one of his stablemates.

runners.comment: Couldn't recommend on hurdle form but ran his best race in a good-ground bumper
runners.spotlight: Unseated quite early in his first two runs over hurdles but finished a remote ninth at Ayr when 150-1; the only positive is the return to a drier surface, as the ground was good when runner-up on bumper debut.

runners.comment: Third in an Irish point; beaten 25l in a bumper and 31 in a maiden hurdle; passed over
runners.spotlight: Third in an Irish point; beaten 25l in a bumper and 31 in a maiden hurdle; passed over.

runners.comment: Never dangerous from off the pace when sixth in a Wetherby bumper (15-2)
runners.spotlight: Never dangerous from off the pace when sixth in a Wetherby bumper (good to soft; 15-2); one of three runners for the yard.

runners.breeder: P Coutereel, D Parreau-Delhote & J Charm
runners.comment: The Ludlow win has worked out well and he sets the standard here by some way
runners.spotlight: Ran on well to win at Ludlow two months ago (soft) and three of the next four home have won since; sets the standard here by some way.

runners.breeder: D Dunbar, R Binnie & P Spence
runners.comment: 125-1 when tailed off in a heavy-ground bumper at Ayr in January
runners.spotlight: 125-1 when tailed off in a heavy-ground bumper at Ayr in January.

prev_owners.owner: David Brennan & Miss K McGivern & Ms J Morgan & Thomas Hore

runners.comment: Minor Flat form in six Irish starts for two different trainers; opposable
runners.spotlight: Minor Flat form in six Irish starts for two different trainers; wouldn't be the obvious solution.

runners.comment: Useful Flat maiden in Ireland and joined this strong yard for 40,000gns
runners.spotlight: No wins in six on the Flat for Jessica Harrington but showed a fair level of ability at up to 1m4f and joined this yard for 40,000gns; lacks jumping experience but raw ability is respected.

racecards.verdict: This looks all about MISTERDOC who had subsequent winners behind him when doing it nicely at Ludlow two months ago.
racecards.betting_forecast: 4/9 Misterdoc, 3/1 Sears Crossing, 10/1 Eustace Grenier,  Mr Maximillian, 20/1 Palavar, 33/1 C'Mon So, 66/1 Jet Noir, 200/1 Jack Dempsey,  Brewdog

racecards.race_name: QuinnBet Highland National Handicap Chase (For The Julian Llewellen Palmer Memorial Trophy) (GBB)

runners.comment: Last seen tailed off in an Irish claiming hurdle; needs a revival and has topweight
runners.spotlight: 3-24 over hurdles and 1-8 as a chaser; left Gavin Cromwell after finishing tailed off in a claiming hurdle in early March (tried blinkers); needs a revival and he's got a lot of weight.

quotes.race: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Rated Novice Chase
quotes.quote: Noble Birth got a freebie in front but he jumped great. We'll see what the handicapper does, maybe the good novice handicap chase at Navan will be a race for him - Gavin Cromwell, trainer

stable_tour.quote: He's been placed in a couple of bumpers and went over hurdles for the first time at Punchestown on Saturday. I didn't think he jumped well enough on the day but he'll be okay and probably needs a bit of a trip. 15-11-21

runners.comment: 100-1 third at Haydock and if as good again here he could have some say
runners.spotlight: Had smart form when with Gordon Elliott before losing his way and selling for £3,000; fell midrace on stable debut but, with the cheekpieces back on, he outran odds of 100-1 to finish a fairly close third at Haydock (3m4f, good); if as good again here then he could have some say.

quotes.race: QuinnBet Grand National Trial Handicap Chase (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Fortunedefortunata is a grand horse. He had a light weight on his back and liked that ground. He travelled away and jumped well, bar the last obviously. It looked like he was after throwing it away at the last, but he did well to get back up after the mistake he made - Ian 'Busty' Amond, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: Kirby Group Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: Fortunedefortunata travelled well and the few hurdles we jumped, he jumped well. He seemed to do it nicely so hopefully he'll keep progressing - Denis O'Regan, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: He won the Grand National Trial at Punchestown last season and went on to run well in the Midlands National at Uttoxeter. He's only eight and you'd like to think there might be another nice handicap chase in him. He might start off in the Troytown at Navan. 26-10-25

runners.comment: Latest Warwick conqueror (3m5f, good to soft) was completing a hat-trick
runners.spotlight: Dual hurdle winner who is 0-5 over fences but three times runner-up in this discipline and latest Warwick conqueror (3m5f, good to soft) was completing a hat-trick; likely to run well off an untouched mark.

runners.comment: 3m4f chase winner last year and some sign of returning to form on his last run
runners.spotlight: Won a 3m4f handicap chase at Leopardstown in March of last year (yielding); this season hasn't gone so well but it wasn't too bad a run on his return to fences at Downpatrick last time (3m4f; yielding to soft) and unwise to put a line through him.

quotes.race: Dublin National Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Brandt has been lucky and unlucky. He won on the first run for us, but I think he should have two more won since as he fell one day and probably got to the front too soon the last day and got lonely but it's great to get that today. The Ulster National is in a month's time at Downpatrick and if he got into it, that would suit perfect - Cian Collins, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's a big horse who jumps very well and I think he'll improve on what he showed at Punchestown last week. 18-10-22

runners.comment: Superior hurdle form is reflected in this lower chase mark; still entitled to run well
runners.spotlight: Superior hurdle form is reflected in this lower chase mark; 0-8 in this discipline but was third over 3m4f at Leopardstown before pulling up in a Listed handicap at Navan; no surprise to see him run well as drying ground won't faze him.

quotes.race: St. Peter's Dunboyne GAA Maiden Hurdle (Div I)
quotes.quote: Gringo D'Aubrelle is a nice horse that probably wants 2m4f. I love the way he put his head down and battled the whole way up the straight - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: This chap is well handicapped. I think he's better than a 115-rated chaser for sure. He hasn't been easy to train but when he puts it all together there's a day in him. 26-10-25

runners.comment: Runner-up in this 12 months ago and returns in form; in the mix off a competitive mark
runners.spotlight: Only 1-21 overall and clearly hard to win with, but he was runner-up in this 12 months ago and returns in form having been running well from 2m4f to 3m; in the mix.

runners.owner: Bedford & Noel & The Can't Say No
runners.comment: Hosed up at Warwick and could take some beating if the ground is bordering on good
runners.spotlight: If the ground is bordering on good then this 8yo could take some beating as he hosed up at Warwick last month (3m, good) on his second run after a break; the 8lb rise isn't the end of the world.

runners.breeder: O Triboire & S C E A Ecurie Des Jap
runners.comment: Raised 8lb for his Sedgefield romp but had become very well handicapped
runners.spotlight: Not as good as he was but has turned a corner following wind surgery and came home clear at Sedgefield (3m2f, good); that race fell apart in behind but he would probably have won anyway; raised 8lb but had become very well handicapped.

quotes.race: Lloyds Animal Feeds Open Hunters' Chase (For The Ludlow Gold Cup)
quotes.quote: He's a lovely horse, a proper horse. I couldn't understand it when Stratagem pulled up at Hereford, he didn't jump or travel. He beat Solo at Auteuil and goes well at home. That was more like it today - David Maxwell, jockey.

quotes.race: Terry Frame Joiners Juvenile Hurdle (Northern Lights Juvenile Hurdle Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: Stratagem probably needed the race first time and he made a bit of a noise so he'll probably need a wind operation in the summer. This is probably a very nice horse, we may put him away and he'll go chasing next season - owner/jockey David Maxwell.

stable_tour.quote: I thought he'd put up a big performance at Cheltenham in October but he was run off his feet. He's only a four-year-old but I think he's now ready for fences, so he's due to run in a novice chase over 2m3f or 2m4f. I'm sure he's a nice horse. 16-11-20

We'll probably aim him at a veterans' chase at Cartmel and let him take his chance alongside Fairlawn Flyer. I'll probably follow the same route as well with him and take him to Perth for the Highlands National too. We want as many runners at Cartmel as we can. 26-03-26

runners.comment: Sound jumper who stays well and he's won three of his last four; progressive
runners.spotlight: Only defeat in his last four races came in a good-quality 3m4f handicap at Windsor; jumped well and stayed on best at Chepstow last time (2m7f, soft) where the front two pulled well clear; raised 7lb but Ned Fox takes away 3lb out of that; respected.

runners.comment: Pulled up two runs back but solid efforts in defeat on either side of that; assured stayer
runners.spotlight: Pulled up two runs ago but solid efforts in defeat on either side of that and he's an assured stayer at this trip; the blinkers are new, as were the cheekpieces when third at Kelso last month.

quotes.race: BK Racing Hexham Marathon Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: There was a question mark over the trip but when Breeze Of Wind hit the front he pricked his ears - Sam Coltherd, jockey.

runners.comment: Expensive to follow over fences and fair to say that others arrive here in better form
runners.spotlight: Dual hurdle winner; has been expensive to follow over fences (0-9) and fair to say that others arrive here in better form.

quotes.race: Maximum Eco For Sustainability Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: President Scottie is a nice, improving horse. He handled a bit of soft ground and he stays well. I don't know how far up the ladder he will go, but he's an unfurnished horse. He'll have another run and Ayr might suit him - Nicky Richards, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He improved with each of his three bumper runs last season and the form suggests they weren't bad races. Sometimes it's about how they finish in bumpers and he should come forward for the education. He's by Milan, so he should stay well, and he'll be novice hurdling. I'd imagine we'll be up to 3m by the spring. 25-10-23

runners.comment: Four wins this season; unproven over this far and he does race up with the pace
runners.spotlight: Went chasing last summer and he's won four times from 3m to 3m2f; now high in the ratings but still ran very well from the front at Carlisle last month (3m); unproven over this far and he does race up with the pace.

stable_tour.quote: We've been waiting for soft ground for him. He'd been running okay on good ground but needs a trip on soft going. There are a lot of handicap hurdle options coming for him now. 11-12-24

racecards.verdict: A chance is taken on Irish raider BRANDT, an assured stayer who signalled a return to form last time at Downpatrick.
racecards.betting_forecast: 100/30 Fever Dream, 5/1 Busty Boy, 13/2 Express Surprise, 7/1 El Granjero,  Stratagem, 8/1 Upfordebate, 9/1 President Scottie, 10/1 Brandt,  Breeze Of Wind, 20/1 Fortunedefortunata, 33/1 Noble Birth

racecards.race_name: Perth Racecourse Racing & Events Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Positive last run; looks sure to stay this far and has the assistance of Sean Bowen
runners.spotlight: A winner the last time he contested a Class 3 handicap (on reappearance) and he was boxing on when beaten a little under 10l in a deep Uttoxeter handicap last time out (2m7f, soft); looks sure to stay this far and has the assistance of Sean Bowen.

runners.breeder: E A R L Ecurie Des Mottes
runners.comment: Justified market support last time; raised 6lb but appeals as a horse with more to offer
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 7yo who was very well backed at Carlisle three weeks ago and ran out a ready winner (3m1f, good to soft); raised 6lb but appeals as a horse with more to offer.

runners.comment: Poor last time and inconsistent; his pretty good record when fresh heightens interest
runners.spotlight: After a brief stint over fences he got back on track in beating 14 rivals over 3m at Windsor (soft) under a positive ride; however, there was a further reminder of his inconsistency when he dropped away tamely at Haydock in February; what does heighten interest is a pretty good record when fresh.

quotes.race: Weatherbys Racing Bank Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Go To War has been chasing and wasn't enjoying it but I think we know why now because he loved being out in front there. It's taken me a year and a half to find the key and that was great - Nicky Henderson, trainer.

quotes.race: Balfours Llp And Lycetts Insurance Novices' Hurdle (Novices' Championship Hurdle Series Qual') (GBB)
quotes.quote: The wind-op has definitely helped. Go To War came under pressure a little bit sooner the last day, but today he travelled, jumped well and I was very pleased with him. The way he did it from the second-last was very good - Fergal O'Brien, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won two hurdle races the season before last but then found it quite hard last season, although he was always threatening. We thought he'd go well on his last run at Newbury but he finished lame and we found he had a fracture in his near-fore joint. He's well now though, and will likely go novice chasing. He stays well. 21-10-25

runners.owner: Mrs Jo Tracey, K Alexander & Russell

prev_owners.owner: Mrs Jo Tracey, K Alexander, P&S Bryceland

runners.comment: Gregor Walkingshaw gets a tune out of him and returning to hurdles looks a good thing
runners.spotlight: Well beaten/pulled up over fences on his last two starts but has each-way claims on the pick of his form over hurdles this season and Gregor Walkingshaw gets a tune out of him.

quotes.race: Karaoke At The Golf Inn Prestwick Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Whistle Stop Tour is a really progressive 7yo and Derek [Fox] was really positive about him after his Kelso win. He has plenty of options open to him. There's the 3m6f novice handicap chase at Cheltenham, there's a nice race at Uttoxeter soon after or there's always the Scottish National back here. Our dream though would be the 2026 Grand National - Sean Tracey, joint-owner, talking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He ran some big races last year before everything went wrong in the Ultima when he was nearly brought down. We tried to rescue the season after that, but he's come back in great form. He looks so much stronger and you'd like to think he'd be a type who could build into a Scottish National horse. He stays very well. 29-10-25

runners.comment: Beginning to look a tricky ride and she's very risky at the minute
runners.spotlight: Ran no race over hurdles on final run for previous yard (tried a visor) and again looked a tricky ride back over fences on debut for this one; the return of cheekpieces may help but she's very risky at the minute.

quotes.race: Molson Coors Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Musique De Fee is so tough. I never run horses that quickly again and she looked really green on Saturday and like she was not having it, but she came out of it lively. She doesn't know how to lose, but I thought turning in we'd be second. Josh [Bryan, jockey] was tactically brilliant, and she stuck her neck out and had her head down when it really mattered - Georgina Nicholls, trainer.

quotes.race: DragonBet: Oncourse And Online Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: I must say a big thank-you to Sean Bowen, who rode Musique De Fee six days ago. I rang him this morning and all he said was to kick on with her and he was right - Finn Lambert, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: The potential is there to be competitive off this mark on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Last run too bad to be true but had been consistent in novice/maidens and the previous third at Musselburgh (3m, good to soft) came in a strong race; the potential is there to be competitive off this mark on handicap debut.

runners.comment: Raised 9lb for winning at Bangor (2m7f) but that was as easy as you like
runners.spotlight: Hadn't shown any benefit for joining Dan Skelton but he put that right when stepped back up in trip at Bangor (2m7f, good), where he won pretty much as he liked after attracting heavy support; 9lb higher this time in a better race but clearly a likely contender.

runners.comment: Front-runner; hat-trick bid came up shy and others in here might be better treated
runners.spotlight: Front-runner; having his 40th career start but a first over 3m when successful at Taunton and he followed up at Plumpton (3m1f; again good to soft); subsequent defeat, again under Murray Dodd, suggests others in here might be better treated.

runners.breeder: Dr V Roger-Yves Simon Et Al
runners.comment: Useful novice but with her unraced beyond 2m5f there are some stamina doubts over this far
runners.spotlight: Bumper and dual hurdles winner; penalties have been finding her out so handicaps now look a better option, but with her unraced beyond 2m5f there are some stamina doubts over this far.

quotes.race: weatherbysshop.co.uk EBF Mares' "National Hunt" Novices' Hurdle (EBF Mares' NH Nov Hdl Qual') (GBB)
quotes.quote: La Zoubida got stuck in the ground a little bit and had a big penalty. She had one or two hard races, but she'll make a lovely chaser next year and that's where you'll see the best of her.  - Nicky Richards, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: She won her first two starts this season over hurdles at Sedgefield and Kelso. She then dropped back in trip at Haydock in a 2m3f Listed mares' hurdle on the Saturday before Christmas and we were very disappointed with her. The ground was probably a bit fast for her and she probably wants another half a mile. I'll put a line through that run - she got pushed out wide and the race just didn't pan out for her. Before that she'd won a bumper and a couple of hurdles, so she hasn't done a lot wrong. She'll be back again - she isn't done yet. 31-12-25

runners.comment: Had a break since bleeding last time and he's still unexposed as a stayer
runners.spotlight: His first run at about 3m when winning at Newcastle (good to soft) and then ran second at Warwick; latest Musselburgh run wasn't too shoddy given he was held up off the pace before staying on and he reportedly bled that day; had a break since and wouldn't be fully exposed as a stayer.

runners.breeder: Sc Racing Investment Society Ecurie Ris
runners.comment: On career-high mark, off which he was no match for the front two on stable debut at Bangor
runners.spotlight: Won races for Dan Skelton (2m1f/2m3f) and Olly Murphy (3m1f); now on a career-high mark, off which he was no match for the front two on stable debut at Bangor (2m7f).

quotes.race: Betano Boosted Odds Every UK Race Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Stayers Hurdle Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: It is brilliant to beat my personal best of 180 last season, I thought last season went amazingly well and this season has gone even better so hopefully I can now reach the next milestone of 200 winners before the end of the campaign. - Sean Bowen, jockey.

runners.comment: Won this last year off the same mark but he ran no race last time at Warwick
runners.spotlight: Had lots of racing in Ireland before joining this yard last year; returned from a wind operation to win this 12 months ago off this very mark but he's an 11yo now and his last two runs, over fences and hurdles, weren't that encouraging.

quotes.race: Cavan Developments Home Builders Supporting St. Mary's GAA Novice Handicap Chase
quotes.quote: Wa Wa stays well, the further he went the better. He liked the ground and kept going, he will go further going forward and is going the right way - Dermot McLoughlin, trainer

runners.comment: Ffos Las return was encouraging given the time he'd been absent and the soft conditions
runners.spotlight: Last season he won 3m handicaps at Doncaster and Wetherby (both on good ground); his Ffos Las return was encouraging given the time he'd been absent and the soft conditions; in this scenario he's unexposed; considered.

stable_tour.quote: He's been a very immature horse and has taken a while to get his act together, but he won his last two races last season. After the last of those, at Wetherby, he had a problem with one of his knees and we've had to deal with that in the summer, so he'll be out a bit later. He loves soft ground and will jump fences. 21-10-25

racecards.verdict: Handicap debutant SLEEDAGH and the unexposed Jupiter Des Mottes appeal most in an open race.
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 Jupiter Des Mottes, 6/1 Roaring Conquest, 15/2 Jukebox Fury, 8/1 Go To War, 9/1 La Zoubida,  Gwennie May Star, 10/1 Sleedagh,  Inferno Sacree, 12/1 Highland Fashion,  Wa Wa, 16/1 Whistle Stop Tour,  Musique De Fee

racecards.race_name: Join Racing TV Now Novices' Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners.breeder: S Shiel, D Savage & T Nolan
runners.owner: Mrs Isobel Webb & Mrs Julie Fowler
runners.comment: Ran well to be third in a Class 3 at Newbury that didn't go entirely like clockwork
runners.spotlight: Went up 5lb for beating an exposed rival at Southwell (2m4f, soft; fine on good to soft) but he still ran well in a Class 3 at Newbury (2m6f) that didn't go entirely like clockwork; he could yet raise his bar higher; much respected.

stable_tour.quote: He came back from injury only to fall at Haydock and I probably ran him too soon afterwards when he went to Huntingdon. So it was an excellent effort to come second when tackling 2m7f for the first time. He'll have a short break to freshen him up and then it's onwards and hopefully upwards. He's a big horse, a good jumper and a progressive staying chaser. 07-01-26

runners.comment: Out of form and much depends whether this return to better ground can inspire
runners.spotlight: Back-to-back wins over similar trips to this last September and on good or yielding ground that he's not had in his last four races; however, current wellbeing is an issue and so too the blinkers in which he was tailed off last time when first fitted.

runners.comment: Probably better again in defeat last time but a 2lb rise is mean given he was beaten 10l
runners.spotlight: Much better chaser than hurdler, winning Class 5s at Catterick (3m1f) and Wetherby (3m; again on soft); wouldn't have beaten the winner in a Class 3 at Bangor even had he not clouted the last fence but that was still a fine run; 2lb rise is a bit mean given he was beaten 10l.

runners.breeder: E A R L De La Cauvelliere

runners.comment: As good as ever two runs ago; now in cheekpieces; drying ground would be a concern
runners.spotlight: Well beaten over a marathon trip last time but looked as good as ever when winning at Doncaster (3m, soft) two starts ago; must have a chance in first-time cheekpieces, though may not be favoured by the drying ground.

runners.comment: Last to finish at Carlisle and it could be that the handicapper has caught up with her
runners.spotlight: Shot up 16lb for her back-to-back wins (2m3f/2m5f) and, although a bad mistake was no help when last to finish at Carlisle, it could be that the handicapper has caught up with her.

quotes.race: Livescore Bet Best Odds Daily Handicap Hurdle (Div II)
quotes.quote: Celestial Fashion likes to bowl along. She's settled down and has improved from it - Ian Duncan, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: QuinnBet Best Odds Guaranteed Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: It's great to get a win on Celestial Fashion because it's taken a little bit of time for her to learn to race and see her races out. She's been second the last twice, probably to a couple of horses that have been a bit progressive and ahead of their marks - Joe Williamson, rider.

runners.comment: Winning chase debut last June; long absence is perhaps a greater concern than the 4lb rise
runners.spotlight: Won an uncompetitive novice hurdle (2m6f, good) last May and the following month made a successful chase debut at Hexham (3m, good to soft); a long absence is perhaps a greater concern than the 4lb rise.

stable_tour.quote: She'll probably be ready, like a lot of ours, for Perth's big meeting at the end of April. She's in great form now, having needed a break. She's strengthened up a lot and she'll win a few races during the summer. She will be a hell of a lot better chasing than over hurdles, as jumping is her main asset. 26-03-26

runners.comment: Respectable runs in handicap hurdles; dual point winner who could do better over fences
runners.spotlight: Six-race maiden over hurdles but ran respectably in his handicaps and this dual point winner could well do better over fences; has been off since January but one to consider, especially if at all strong in the betting.

runners.comment: Won over hurdles off a similar mark but his chase form lacks a bit of substance
runners.spotlight: Placed in a 3m Irish point but has never raced beyond about 2m over jumps; won over hurdles off a similar mark but his chase form lacks a bit of substance.

racecards.verdict: The vote goes to HE KNOWS BETTER who still looks progressive over fences despite his defeat at Newbury.
racecards.betting_forecast: 15/8 All Inn Hand, 3/1 He Knows Better, 4/1 Dixie Mafia, 5/1 Celestial Fashion, 10/1 Solly Attwell,  Rock On Jet

racecards.race_name: Follow @racingtv On Instagram Handicap Hurdle

runners.comment: Won six on the spin in 2024 but pulled up on belated reappearance in February
runners.spotlight: On a roll in the second half of 2024, rattling off six straight wins (2m5f-3m1f), but pulled up on belated return at Kelso at the end of February; entitled to strip fitter but can still only watch.

quotes.race: Albert Bartlett Novices' Hurdle (Registered As The Bristol Novices' Hurdle) (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was probably just one run too many and I'm not sure it's his track, Skyjack Hijack would probably be better at Aintree. That said I'm glad we've come now and not come and had a hard race in March. He'll have a break until the spring now and then I'll come back for a bit better ground, we could go to the River Don. He's off for a holiday now but he's still a superstar - Jennie Candlish, trainer.

quotes.race: Weatherbys nhstallions.co.uk 'The French Furze' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Skyjack Hijack has done great and keeps at a good gallop - his jumping is his biggest asset. I honestly think the way he jumps he reminds me of a Champion Hurdle horse. He's so quick and accurate.  How high can we go? He's doing everything right. I suppose Cheltenham comes into the equation and we can see whether we go in handicaps or down the Albert Bartlett route. It takes a fair horse to win six in a row and they were decent horses he beat too. He goes that gallop and he gets horses beat a long way out. It's great to have a horse like him.  That'll be it for a while, he's been busy and the ground's going to start to change. After having a chat with Sean, he said he wasn't fully on song today. All these indicate he needs a break now and we won't see him until February time - Alan O'Keeffe, trainer's assistant.

quotes.race: Southwest Rail Solutions Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: There's an Albert Bartlett qualifier at Cheltenham next month and I think we'll consider having a crack at that. You never know if they will go at Cheltenham, so we might run Skyjack Hijack in the qualifier, give him a break and then come back for the big one. He was up against better quality horses today and he's improved again - Alan Baxter, owner.

quotes.race: Download The Quinnbet App Handicap Hurdle (Go North Brindisi Breeze Series Qualifier)
quotes.quote: I didn't want to go too quick early on as it was only four days since Skyjack Hijack last ran and, although I knew he won really well at Aintree, he was all out at the line. He's not a slow horse and has got a great cruising speed but this step up to three miles has been the making of him. We always thought he wanted cut in the ground but he seems to love this good ground - Sean Quinlan, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

quotes.race: Barrie Wells Trust Box4Kids Conditional Jockeys' Handicap Hurdle (Challenger Stayers' Hurdle Qual')
quotes.quote: His confidence is coming. Skyjack Hijack was very good at Perth last time and likes this better ground. He jumps, stays and is very uncomplicated. It's definitely on the radar [Newcastle on Thursday] and he seems fine coming back in, so hopefully he'll be okay to run again. He'll go there without penalty and we'll have a chat with the owners - Alan O'Keeffe, Assistant Trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's been a real revelation, winning his last six races. The latest win was at Newcastle last Saturday in the French Furze, which he won by nine and a half lengths. Since winning a low-grade, soft-ground handicap hurdle at Cartmel in August, the trajectory has been incredible. His jumping has been a joy - he jumps so quickly out of quick ground. He probably won't run now until the new year and he'll probably be targeted at the River Don at Doncaster on January 25. It's a 3m novice hurdle worth £75,000. If he's good enough to warrant his place in the field, the long-term ambition would be the Albert Bartlett at the Cheltenham Festival. I have to mention what a big help it is having Sean Quinlan on board. He's a huge part of the team in getting to know the horses, school them and then ride them. 05-12-24

runners.breeder: N J Henderson And Mrs S A Aston
runners.comment: Below par since win in December but potential class act for yard with good record in this
runners.spotlight: Added to his excellent Sandown record when winning over 2m on soft in December; below par since, including a never-dangerous seventh when bidding for a third successive Imperial Cup back at Sandown, but this is the first time he's dropped to a Class 3 since winning at Cheltenham in December 2023; yard has won the last two runnings of this.

quotes.race: Bet At Your Best With Betfair Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Go Dante needs to race and we couldn't bring him back for the Imperial Cup fresh, so I'm chuffed to bits. He loves it around here on soft ground and is a star. We'd better try to come back to win another Imperial Cup - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Imperial Cup Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I've learned in a short period of time in training that you've got to have a plan, and that plan has come off today. I thought Go Dante was just starting to click and he loves this place. He's had a very tough race like he did last year and we'll see how he is in the morning. I'd imagine he probably won't run [at Cheltenham], but today was his main target and it's job done as far as I'm concerned - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfair Imperial Cup Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It gives me an awful lot of satisfaction. A lot of work has gone into Go Dante. He broke his pelvis in a Challow Hurdle and we gave him a load of time off, then he had a schooling accident and damaged a lung, which kept him out for another few months. He's massively given me headaches - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: Catesby Estates Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: This has been a long time coming. I'm not surprised. Go Dante is one of those horses that every time he runs I go racing thinking that he'll win. I considered going to Ascot [for the Betfair Exchange Trophy] just before Christmas with him, but we decided to come here and I'm delighted. There's part of me that thinks I wish I had waited to go to Ascot for a bigger prize, but it's Barbara's [Hester, owner] first Cheltenham winner and that is brilliant. Something like a Betfair Hurdle is what we could look at. He has loads of ability - Olly Murphy, trainer.

quotes.race: Happy 41st Birthday Hazel Rofe Maiden Open National Hunt Flat Race (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I don't know if we'll see Go Dante again this season. Aintree might be a tiny possibility, but he won't run under a penalty somewhere. He's a big raw horse and is a smart prospect - Olly Murphy, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He was brilliant in winning the Imperial Cup for the second time; whether he's able to land three remains to be seen. Now a year older, at two miles he's going to want very soft ground, and I wouldn't be afraid to step him up to two and a half before too long. He's definitely handicapped to still be competitive off 131 and I'd love to go back for the Imperial Cup, but he'd need it to be very testing. 23-10-25
He has got plenty of ability but hasn't reached the highs that he should have just yet. We'll start off in a handicap hurdle in the next few 01-11-23

runners.owner: Paddy Brennan Racing Syndicate Jack Hyde
runners.comment: Fourth hurdle win when shading close finish at Ludlow latest; should go well again
runners.spotlight: Didn't feature in the Imperial Cup (Go Dante two places ahead of him) but back on track with his sights lowered when shading a tight finish in 2m Ludlow handicap (good) 25 days ago, taking his hurdles record to 4-12; has won over this trip; should remain very competitive off 6lb higher.

quotes.race: Darnells Dash Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Jack Hyde can be a free-going type, so I was worried he might be fresh after a break. He was a bit keen but he jumps so well you don't mind that. Fergal [O'Brien, trainer] knows the sort of horse you need for that race [Grade 2 Persian War at Chepstow]. He felt good, so there's no reason why not - Tom Broughton, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Well held in Morebattle over 2m but in good form over 2m4f prior to that; should be in mix
runners.spotlight: 9yo who was tailed off at Kelso in February last time but that was the competitive Morebattle Hurdle over 2m; in good form over 2m4f prior to that, winning at Newcastle then second at Aintree (both good to soft); likely to be in the mix back up in trip.

quotes.race: bet365 Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Serious Operator is improving, his jumping was perfect. We were a bit worried about the ground. His hurdling is outstanding and he'll go chasing next season - Lucinda Russell, trainer.

quotes.race: Bet Boost At bet365 Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: When Serious Operator gets his ground and gets everything sorted he's a heck of a horse. He couldn't get out of the heavy ground last time. Today he travelled and I probably got there too soon. I hope he's turned the corner now - Patrick Wadge, rider.

stable_tour.quote: He needs good ground and wasn't quite right last season. The rain came at the wrong time at Aintree, but it was a really encouraging run. We could see him coming good in a big-field handicap hurdle over two and a half miles. 29-10-25

He came to us from Daniel Murphy in Ireland having won two point-to-points. He won first time out for us under rules at Kelso and, after an unhappy run at Cheltenham in October, returned this month with a win over 2m4½f at Newcastle. He's not over-big but has a nice engine and stays exceedingly well. He's better on good to soft. After his Cheltenham run Tom [Scudamore] suggested he had breathing issues and he was subsequently operated on. He won after the operation but genuinely seems better than ever and we could head back to Cheltenham this weekend. He's a strong galloper and jumps well and long term I can't wait to see him novice chasing. 25-01-23

runners.comment: Below par back hurdling latest but had wind op since and stable enjoying a cracking spring
runners.spotlight: Better known as a chaser nowadays, but won twice over hurdles over four years ago; no real promise back hurdling six weeks ago but had wind surgery since and his stable is enjoying a cracking spring.

quotes.race: Weatherbys nhstallions.co.uk Graduation Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We were a little bit wrong in the ratings but I just thought Nells Son wasn't that far out of it and with four runners it was well worth a chance. We'll just take our time and freshen him up again. We'll stick to two miles and he needs a good, strongly run race. Hopefully he'll hold his form well all winter - Nicky Richards, trainer.

quotes.race: KOSB Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Nells Son jumped well and to give credit to the horse, he's probably a different class to them a little bit. On softer ground two miles is maybe far enough for him. On a bit of good ground he probably gets two and a half [miles] well. Hopefully he might just have a nice spring - Nicky Richards, trainer.

quotes.race: Rhino.Bet Novices' Limited Handicap Chase (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Nells Son has very decent form and that was a nice first start back. He might work his way into a decent race at some stage. We know where the M6 is if we need to go down there, but we'll take it as it comes and hopefully we'll have a good season with him - Nicky Richards, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Premier Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We've been building Nells Son up. The trip beat him at Ayr so we dropped him back at Haydock, where we rode him to run a good race. - I thought 'are you as good as I thought you were?' Was I getting it wrong with him altogether? He's fairly ground dependent, he needs a bit of soft ground. The Scottish Champion Hurdle is a possibility, I'll see what the weather's doing. But I said to Sean you'll be seeing this horse at Leopardstown next Christmas. He'll go chasing next season and he'll make a wonderful chaser - Nicky Richards, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: We're not quite sure if he likes that really testing ground and it was hard work last time out when he was third to stablemate Findthetime. He never looked like he was going to win but he's a lot better than that one run and hopefully he'll make up for it as the season goes on. Most horses have a blip now and again, so we like to think he'll bounce back after a little break. 27-11-23

He's had two runs this season and done pretty well both times. He ran well over hurdles at Carlisle and then made a bit of a mistake at the ditch down at the bottom of the hill in a chase at Kelso and that just paid to his chances, but he still didn't run too bad. He may go down to Windsor along with Nab Wood - there's a 2m handicap chase at that meeting that we're sort of thinking about. 31-12-25

runners.comment: Best run since returning from absence when fourth over C&D on Wednesday; more needed now
runners.spotlight: Won four on the trot, all at around 2m4f (good/soft), in 2024; strong in the market and easily best run since returning from a long absence when fourth of seven over C&D (good) on Wednesday; needs to build on that turned out again quickly.

quotes.race: Unibet Persian War Novices' Hurdle (Grade 2) (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Flying Fortune has taken a while to get the hang of things but is a good mare. She has a lovely attitude and has been very straightforward to train. Her mother [Turbo Linn] was very good and at one point was lined up for the Melbourne Cup. We'll go home and scour the programme book but I don't imagine we will run her again until Christmas. She's been busy and could do with six weeks off. We would have to look at the Mares' Novices' Hurdle in March - she's won that in a canter really - Peter Bowen, trainer.

quotes.race: Dragonbet Fixed Brush Hurdle Series Final Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Flying Fortune has been a star and looks like a different mare since we first got her. She's getting better and better. It's definitely our biggest win together. It'd be great if we could have more contests like this and she'll go to the Silver Trophy next at Chepstow. She's earned her place in a race like that - Michael Bowen, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Unibet Moneyback As Cash Races Handicap Hurdle
quotes.quote: This was the plan all along. We were a bit disappointed to be beaten last time, but the form of that has obviously been boosted in the first race, and I thought Flying Fortune's mark was great. She'll be going round the likes of Perth and Cartmel this summer - Mickey Bowen, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She's disappointed twice now since she's been back from an injury, but I think it's ground related. If you go back through her form, she's not got anything on testing going - she got beaten in a maiden hurdle at Southwell on soft ground by a horse who was rated just over 100. She's not half the filly unless she's got quick ground and we're waiting for it to come. If it's right for her and she gets in, we may find something for her at Aintree and have a go. 26-03-26

runners.comment: Second to Grade 2 winner before seeing off next-time-out winners at Market R; promising
runners.spotlight: Won a 3m maiden point at Alnwick in December and promising start over hurdles, chasing home a subsequent Grade 2 winner from the Willie Mullins yard at Carlisle before seeing off two next-time-out winners when landing a maiden at Market Rasen (2m4f, good to soft); a very interesting handicap newcomer.

prev_owners.owner: Mrs A Frost & R H Fowler & Jon Owen & Oliver Slipper

runners.comment: Weakened quickly and pulled up over C&D on Thursday
runners.spotlight: Clear promise in both hurdle starts for Lorna Fowler in Ireland prior to £54,000 sale; won a Fakenham maiden (2m4f, good to soft) on stable debut in January; creditable fourth of 11 at Uttoxeter (2m7f, good to soft) four weeks ago but weakened quickly and pulled up over C&D on Thursday.

runners.comment: Not at best this term but not disgraced latest and well treated if staging revival
runners.spotlight: Three wins last season; hasn't scaled the same heights this time round, although latest third of six at Newcastle was a bit more encouraging and he's well handicapped if staging a full-scale revival.

quotes.race: LiveScore Bet Best Odds Daily Hogmaneigh Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Bold Light was sold for £50,000 three years ago, but when he was taken home the owner found out he had a hole in his leg, so took him back to the sales. I then bought him for £1,000 and it turned out to be quite a bad injury, the vet told me it was better to put him out of his misery. We put him out in Ruth Jardine's [sister of trainer Iain] field for three years, and it's done the world for him. He's been fantastic ever since, we couldn't complain at all. After he finished third at Haydock we were scratching our heads and wondering where to go, we came here and the next plan will be the Scottish County Hurdle here on February 1. We think we'll stick to hurdles because we want to look after him  - James Scott, owner.

runners.comment: Returned from absence to win over C&D on Thursday; 7lb penalty if out again quickly
runners.spotlight: Returned from a long absence to justify favouritism over C&D (good) on Thursday, coming from off the pace to hit the front when left clear at the last; will carry a 7lb penalty if turned out again quickly.

quotes.race: Dragonbet Fixed Brush Hurdle Series Final Novices' Handicap Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Letterston Lily should become a lovely horse. We only ran her because it was such a big race and it'll be about next spring for her. She could be an exciting filly - Michael Bowen, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Hadwins Mares' Novices' Hurdle (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted with Letterston Lily. She jumped absolutely superbly. She's always worked brilliantly. She was a bit green at Aintree but she ran a blinder that day. Hopefully there's a bit more to come. She's got a fair turn of foot, that's why we put her in the Aintree bumper, and she showed it there today -  joint-trainer Peter Bowen, speaking on Racing TV.

racecards.verdict: If there's one in this line-up which could be well ahead of its mark it's the promising 6yo THE DOG THIEF (nap).
racecards.betting_forecast: 3/1 The Dog Thief, 7/2 Letterston Lily, 9/2 Jack Hyde, 7/1 Go Dante,  Serious Operator, 11/1 Flying Fortune, 12/1 Bold Light, 14/1 Nells Son, 20/1 Skyjack Hijack,  King Jon Oliver

racecards.race_name: One Place. Every Race. Racing TV Novices' Handicap Hurdle (Div I)

runners.comment: Recent AW Flat efforts no more than respectable ahead of hurdle return
runners.spotlight: Easily best effort in four maiden/novice hurdles last season when second at Newcastle (2m1f, good to soft); did manage back-to-back wins over 2m on the Flat at Catterick last May but more recent AW Flat efforts have been no more than respectable.

quotes.race: Hillcrest Who Cares Wins Handicap
quotes.quote: I didn't ride Zephyln last time and it was very tactical. It's not the way he needs riding. The favourite and second favourite got the run of the race at Ayr and it turned into a sprint. He's a horse you need to be going flat out from the get go - Jason Hart, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Easy win on Exeter handicap debut last Friday; will take a bit of stopping in  same mood
runners.spotlight: Barely had to be nudged out to make a winning start to his handicap career at Exeter (2m2f, good) last Friday; the extra yardage here should help if anything and he'll take a bit of stopping under a 7lb penalty if showing up in a similar mood.

runners.comment: Only fair fourth on handicap debut but still early days for top yard which does well here
runners.spotlight: No immediate improvement for a switch to handicap company when fourth of nine over 2m5f at Haydock (good to soft) seven weeks ago but it's still early days for a good stable with a very strong Perth record.

runners.comment: Disappointing last twice but undergone wind surgery ahead of handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Disappointing in maiden hurdles on his last two outings but showed a bit of promise in similar races prior to that and has had wind surgery ahead of this handicap debut; also refitted with the tongue-tie he wore in bumpers.

runners.comment: Very lightly raced but betting best guide now handicapping for new yard after absence
runners.spotlight: Hurdling debut fourth at Market Rasen in November 2024 but she failed to build on it in two subsequent runs for Dr Richard Newland and Jamie Insole; remains very lightly raced so she may still do better on her yard and handicap debut after 14 months off; also wears first-time cheekpieces.

runners.comment: No improvement when 14.5fl third on handicap debut latest but it's still early days
runners.spotlight: Failed to improve on his maiden/novice form when 14.5l third of ten on Bangor handicap debut (2m3f, good) five weeks ago; still early days but he'll need to step up on that effort to go close here.

runners.comment: Made all over 2m4f at Ayr; only fifth over 2m there since but may fare better back at 2m4f
runners.spotlight: Low-mileage 7yo who made all and held on narrowly from Velvet Vulcan in conditional jockeys' race at Ayr (2m4f, soft) in February; not in the same form when fifth over 2m back at Ayr since but the return to 2m4f may see him in a better light.

runners.comment: Modest form in qualifying runs but more realistic chance now handicapping
runners.spotlight: Modest form in three qualifying runs (trained in Ireland first two) but more realistic chance now handicapping for a yard which had a winner at Kelso on Monday.

runners.comment: Two near misses at Ayr this year (to The Coffey Boy latterly) but below par last twice
runners.spotlight: Dual Flat winner who showed best hurdles form when going very close at Ayr (2m4f, soft) in January/February, latterly to The Coffey Boy; does need to shrug off two lesser runs since, though.

quotes.race: BetUK. Home Of The Acca Classified Stakes
quotes.quote: We're very happy for owner-breeder Richard Marriott and his broodmare Battery Power. Velvet Vulcan is now the fourth winner from the mare from four runners - Michael Keady, joint-trainer.

runners.comment: Well treated on novice third in March but been able to confirm it in two handicaps since
runners.spotlight: Improved third in 2m1f Carlisle novice (soft) in February; well treated on that form but hasn't managed to reproduce it in two subsequent handicaps, although he probably pressed for home too far out when third back at Carlisle (2m3f, good to soft) in refitted cheekpieces (retained) three weeks ago; remains one who could click from a lowly mark.

runners.comment: Has offered little in three runs this term, including back from break this month
runners.spotlight: Modest maiden hurdler; has offered little in his three runs this term, weakening into a well-held seventh back from a break at Sedgefield 23 days ago.

runners.comment: Well beaten in two 3m handicaps seven months apart; off for a further 101 days
runners.spotlight: Well beaten on 3m course handicap debut last June (final start for Gary Rutherford) and fared little better for new yard at Ayr (3m again) seven months later; hopes are pinned on a shorter trip helping after a further 101 days off.

racecards.verdict: If MR JUKEBOX is in anything like the same form as when winning readily on last week's handicap debut he'll take a bit of stopping.
racecards.betting_forecast: 13/8 Mr Jukebox, 5/1 Berkenshtaaap, 9/1 Walk On Son,  The Coffey Boy,  King Kodiak, 10/1 Valette, 11/1 Zephlyn,  Velvet Vulcan, 12/1 Pepite De Saphir, 25/1 Seeyainthesuninn, 33/1 Nae Bother At A'

racecards.race_name: One Place. Every Race. Racing TV Novices' Handicap Hurdle (Div II)

runners.comment: Bumper winner; fair third on two of four hurdle starts; handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Won a Kelso bumper in November 2024 (2m, good to soft); fair third in a novice hurdle there (2m6f, good to soft) on second jumps start; hasn't reproduced it in two subsequent outings but may fare better now switching to a handicap.

runners.comment: Non-runner
runners.spotlight: Ex-Irish 6yo; initially disappointing for new stable this year but was made odds-on favourite at Newcastle (2m4f, good to soft) last month and won readily; even a 9lb rise may not stop him now he's up and running for Dan Skelton; non-runner.

runners.comment: Well beaten on last month's Carlisle handicap debut; tongue-tie worn then quickly removed
runners.spotlight: Record of 0-5 in Irish points and 0-4 under rules; took keen hold and weakened when fitted with a first-time tongue-tie on last month's Carlisle handicap debut; the tongue-tie is quickly removed.

runners.comment: Unconvincing so far but Sean Bowen booked for Irish yard no stranger to Perth success
runners.spotlight: Not beaten far in a Galway bumper on debut; unconvincing hurdles form so far (including well held on completed start in handicaps) but Sean Bowen enlisted by an Irish yard no stranger to Perth success over the years, although not so much in recent times; betting interesting.

runners.comment: Uncomplicated front-runner who gained a first win at Market Rasen 19 days ago; respected
runners.spotlight: A change of headgear (cheekpieces for visor) saw him land a first success at Market Rasen (2m4f, good) 19 days ago; this front-runner seems an uncomplicated type and should give it another good shot off 5lb higher.

runners.comment: Tailed off in hurdle and pulled up in chase this term; plenty to prove in new cheekpieces
runners.spotlight: Point winner; showed a bit in novice hurdles in November 2024 but tailed off in a novice hurdle and pulled up in a handicap chase in two outings this season over four months apart; fitted with first-time cheekpieces back hurdling; plenty to prove at present.

stable_tour.quote: He was disappointing at Hexham last month but then ran better at Ayr behind Evaluation, who was very good on the Flat. He's a nice novice. 21-11-24

runners.breeder: P Mehat & B Mehat & C Lemeunier
runners.comment: Won hurdle last month and fair fourth in chase ten days later; enters calculations
runners.spotlight: Irish bumper winner who got off the mark over hurdles at the ninth attempt in a handicap at Plumpton (2m4f, good to soft) last month; not far off that form when fourth on his Warwick chase debut (2m4f, good) ten days later; enters calculations back hurdling.

prev_owners.owner: Exors Of The Late John Wade

runners.comment: Losing run at 33 and remains to be seen if new headgear combination helps to snap it
runners.spotlight: Only a respectable fourth of five at Sedgefield a fortnight ago, extending his losing run to 33; has a first-time visor added to his regular tongue-tie now.

runners.comment: Well held in three qualifying runs but potential improver now handicapping up in trip
runners.spotlight: Beaten a long way in three qualifying runs over hurdles at up to 2m1f but did hint at promise on the first of two bumper starts and improvement wouldn't be a surprise now handicapping up in trip (bred for further).

runners.comment: Has reached frame in two of three handicaps and down another 2lb here
runners.spotlight: Has reached the frame in two of his three handicaps at around 2m4f this spring and being eased another 2lb can only help.

runners.comment: Promise when third on handicap debut here (3m) on Wednesday, travelling well
runners.spotlight: Irish point winner in November; suffered heavy defeats in his first three hurdles but better signs after wind surgery when third of ten on handicap debut here (3m, good) on Wednesday, with the way he travelled suggesting this drop back in trip may help if anything.

runners.comment: Ran pretty well in his two handicaps (latest yesterday) but is now 8lb out of the handicap
runners.spotlight: Ran pretty well at Newcastle (2m1f) last month and Perth (2m, good) yesterday in his two handicaps, following wind surgery and a layoff; much more is needed, though, from 8lb out of the handicap over this new trip.

racecards.verdict: The suggestion is DE DELI COUNTER on the back of his Market Rasen success.
racecards.betting_forecast: 7/2 De Deli Counter,  Kap De Triomphe, 5/1 Roi Du Roume, 6/1 Humble Jumble,  Poet's Gale, 10/1 Star Vantage, 12/1 Knockeranna Rose, 16/1 Dublinofficecallin, 20/1 Karma De Cotte,  Gorvennec

racecards.race_name: Every Race Live On Racing TV Open National Hunt Flat Race (Category 1 Elimination) (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Bought for £60,000 after finishing second in a point and that form now reads well
runners.spotlight: Bought for £60,000 after finishing second on Irish point debut in November (yielding ground) and that form looks good with the third finishing fourth in the recent Grade 2 at Aintree; respected.

runners.comment: Out of a bumper/2m7f hurdle winner; stable 1-26 in bumpers recent seasons
runners.spotlight: 13,000euros foal; out of a bumper/2m7f hurdle winner; stable 1-26 in bumpers recent seasons.

runners.comment: Placed in good-ground bumpers in summer 2024 but not seen since; tongue-tie added now
runners.spotlight: Placed in two good-ground bumpers in 2024; easy to pick holes in the form of both races and perhaps the stable second string here; tongue-tie added.

runners.comment: Point winner; difficult to know what he achieved at Cork behind an 80-1 winner
runners.spotlight: Did well in Irish points; runner-up in a 2m3f bumper at Cork on yielding ground but the winner was an 80-1 chance who hadn't shown much previously; this 5yo still rates a likely contender with improvement on the cards.

runners.comment: Bought for £85,000 after winning a 3m Irish point on yielding in October 2024
runners.spotlight: Bought for £85,000 after winning a 3m Irish point on yielding in October 2024 and that form has some substance; interesting to see what the market makes of him after such a long absence, especially with the yard doubly represented.

runners.comment: From off the pace he made a promising debut to be beaten 7.5l at Wetherby (soft) in Dec
runners.spotlight: From off the pace he made a promising debut to be beaten 7.5l at Wetherby (soft) in December; second run has been a while coming but has to be of interest for last year's successful yard.

runners.comment: 40-1 and never seriously counted on good ground at Sedgefield earlier this month
runners.spotlight: 40-1 and never seriously counted on good ground at Sedgefield earlier this month; others preferred.

runners.comment: Beaten 4.5l when third in a small-field Irish point in February (heavy)
runners.spotlight: Beaten 4.5l when third in a small-field Irish point in February (heavy); new yard not renowned for winning bumpers but this 4yo evidently has some ability.

runners.comment: Newcomer from a yard that's 0-34 in bumpers the last five seasons
runners.spotlight: Unraced dam out of unraced half-sister to prolific French 2m1f-2m5f hurdle/chase winner Master Flight; from a yard that's 0-34 in bumpers the last five seasons.

runners.comment: Irish stable has bumper winners in Britain; market needs checking
runners.spotlight: Half-brother to winners Jet Setting Johnny (2m4f chase) and Jet To Vegas (useful 2m/2m2f hurdle); Irish stable has bumper winners in Britain; market needs checking.

runners.comment: Tailed off at Down Royal last month and at 50-1 not a lot was seemingly expected of her
runners.spotlight: Tailed off at Down Royal last month and at 50-1 not a lot was seemingly expected of her.

racecards.verdict: When runner-up in an Irish point AR AIS ARIS finished ahead of Merry Away who was fourth in the recent Grade 2 bumper at Aintree.
