racecards.race_name: bet365 Handicap

runners.breeder: Ecurie Haras De Saint Vincent Et Al
runners.comment: 6f maiden/novice wins last year; returns having been gelded; could be suited by drop to 5f
runners.spotlight: Won maiden/novice races at Ayr (6f, good to firm/good) last season on two of his first three starts; came up short in Group/sales races otherwise but reappears having been gelded and he could prove well suited by this first crack at 5f; interesting on handicap debut, especially if backed.

quotes.race: Racing TV Profits Returned To Racing Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Archie [Watson, trainer] has a good handle on these races and a good handle on his speed horses - James Doyle, jockey of Underwriter, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Absent since last July but twice looked good at Chester last summer; handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Won at Chester (6f, good) last June on second start and comfortably followed up in novice there (6f, good) the following month; absent since and this handicap debut is a much tougher test of his credentials, but he's a bright prospect and it remains to be seen where his limitations lie.

stable_tour.quote: He didn't do anything wrong last year but had a setback after his second novice win, which kept him out of action. He'll start back in either the six-furlong Class 2 handicap for three-year-olds at the Craven meeting or the seven-furlong handicap at Newbury's Greenham meeting. He could be fun this season. 01-04-26

runners.comment: Below par on final two starts last term and same story on recent reappearance at Newmarket
runners.spotlight: Two wins last summer for Ger Lyons but down the field in Listed races last autumn on both starts for Charles Byrnes and soundly beaten in a handicap at Newmarket last Thursday on his stable/seasonal debut; others preferred.

quotes.race: Harvertech Maiden
quotes.quote: Like ours do from their first time out, Sir Alfie has come on an awful lot. You do need a run here for experience because it is a trappy 5f. Leigh said that when the other horse got to him, he put his head down like a terrier and fought back and then he couldn't pull him up so there is an extra furlong up his sleeve - Shane Lyons, assistant trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Impressed at Yarmouth when last seen & could have plenty more to offer; yard in good form
runners.spotlight: Built upon last September's debut (5f, AW) to go close at Nottingham (5f, good to soft), then went one better at Yarmouth (5f, good to soft) in October when last seen; he could do with breaking more professionally but he impressed last time and could have plenty more to offer; yard in good form.

quotes.race: British EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: From what I heard they've always thought enough of Atticum, he's just taken maybe a bit of time to learn and come to hand and he's done it pretty easily today - George Wood, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

runners.comment: Won in good style at Newbury last September; well bred and has potential off opening mark
runners.spotlight: Won with something to spare at Newbury (6f, good to soft) last September on second start then pulled hard when mid-division in Listed race at York (6f, good); gelded since, which may settle him down, and this well-bred sort has potential off his opening mark.

quotes.race: Kennet Valley Syndicates Nick Robinson EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Black Star Boy is in the Goffs Million next week, which is worth a fortune, and we bought him with that race in mind. It's probably not the right thing to do because he's such a big horse, but it's half a million euros to the winner so we'll see - Ed Walker, trainer.

runners.comment: Midfield at York last August but close third in nursery at Glorious Goodwood previously
runners.spotlight: Midfield in big-field nursery at York's Ebor meeting (6f, good to firm) last August when last seen; gelded since; however, close third in a nursery at Glorious Goodwood (6f, good to soft) previously, showing good pace, and he's in the picture on that form; also effective on good/good to firm.

quotes.race: bet365 Two Year Old Trophy EBF Conditions Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: That was very straightforward. Old Is Gold has got a great mind, he got me into a lovely position and he relaxed. He travelled into it beautifully and he's a clever horse, he just does enough when he's in front. I hope he'll keep progressing. I don't know plans but I'd imagine he'll go to Ascot. He'd cope with it 100 per cent - he'd probably drive the box there - P J McDonald, jockey.

runners.comment: Won AW maiden last September; attractive pedigree and could take higher order still
runners.spotlight: Built upon the promise of his first two starts (6f, good/AW) when readily winning a Southwell maiden (5f, AW) at odds-on last September; his attractive pedigree provides optimism that he can take higher order still.

runners.comment: Progressive on AW this year, having been gelded; thereabouts if return to turf is no issue
runners.spotlight: 0-5 last year, all on turf, but he showed promise and won a handicap at Southwell (5f, AW) in January on his first run since being gelded; close second at Southwell (5f, AW) a fortnight ago and could be thereabouts if the return to grass isn't an issue.

runners.comment: Some good AW handicap form but he's probably vulnerable against unexposed types
runners.spotlight: Runner-up on debut at Ripon (6f, good) last August and won Kempton novice (6f, AW) in November on fourth start; some good AW handicap efforts since but not last time and he's probably vulnerable against unexposed types.

racecards.verdict: Having been headstrong last year, a gelding operation may be a positive for BLACK STAR BOY, who earns the vote ahead of Atticum.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/4 Calico Blue, 4/1 Black Star Boy, 9/2 Old Is Gold,  Hypnotised, 7/1 Atticum, 9/1 Ambishio, 10/1 Underwriter, 20/1 One And Gone, 50/1 Sir Alfie

racecards.race_name: bet365 Esher Cup Handicap

runners.comment: Good fourth in Group 2 at Goodwood last July but has to prove he can cut it off this mark
runners.spotlight: Won on debut at Salisbury (7f, good to firm) last June and kept on for fourth in Group 2 Vintage Stakes at Goodwood (7f, good) next time; ran okay in quality conditions race at Newbury (1m, good to soft) in September when last seen but he needs to prove he can cut it off this lofty mark.

quotes.race: Dragon Symbol Standing At Whitsbury Manor British EBF Blagrave Maiden Stakes (GBBRace)
quotes.quote: Goodwood Galaxy did everything right. We don't train to win first time out, so we never really go there with a massive expectation. But his work was good and his two working companions have won well in the past few days. He can be a bit opiniated at times, so the plan was to keep it simple. By keeping him happy he kept everyone else happy. He has his quirks and I was told his stallion [Kodi Bear] was the same. He wants to do things his way at times and instead of stopping him from doing them, you have to channel them into positive attitudes - David Menuisier, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He won really well on his debut at Salisbury and his Racing Post Rating of 92 was quite high for a debutant. Looking at previous winners of the Vintage, that rating is usually what horses ran to on their first or second start and he went for that race on Tuesday. Of course there's his name and owners [Goodwood Racehorse Owners Group] and he ran well to be fourth, beaten about two lengths. Nobody was under any illusions that it was a tough race, but it was well worth a go. 30-07-25

runners.comment: Two 2yo wins; failed to stay 1m2f when last seen; the hood could be a positive on return
runners.spotlight: Won Kempton novice (7f, AW) last September on third start and followed up in warm conditions race at Newbury (1m, good to soft); failed to settle and didn't stay 1m2f in Group 3 Zetland Stakes at Newmarket last seen; wind op since and the hood could be a positive on reappearance; chance.

quotes.race: Haynes, Hanson & Clark Conditions Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: It was a nice race without being too deep and I think Look To The Stars showed a good attitude. He kept plugging away and is an improving sort who will go on and probably get further next year. I don't see any reason why he couldn't step up somewhere if he comes out of this okay. Charlie [Appleby, trainer] mentioned possibly the Autumn Stakes, but we'll see where he fits in with the others. I think he'll be a nice horse - Alex Merriam, trainer's assistant.

runners.comment: 2-2 and could have lots more left in the tank for last year's winning yard; key player
runners.spotlight: Impressive on debut at Southwell (7f, AW) last November and made it 2-2 in Yarmouth novice (1m, good) on recent reappearance; his inexperience was still evident last time and this well-bred colt could have lots more left in the tank for last year's winning yard; key player on handicap debut.

quotes.race: Bet £10 Get £40 With BetMGM EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: It was hard not to be impressed. It's Organise's first day at school and it's hard to know what to expect, and he was pretty raw in the paddock, but once I was up on him he was quite professional. In the race he was a bit reactive, he didn't know whether to take a hold or drop the bridle throughout, but once we got balanced up in the straight he quickened up smartly and just ran green in the final furlong. He's learned loads today and hopefully he can be quite smart - James Doyle, jockey.

runners.owner: G C Myddelton, C F E Hill & Partner
runners.comment: Won small-field nursery over C&D last September but makes reappearance off 13lb higher
runners.spotlight: Won Ripon novice (1m, good to firm) last August on third start then followed up in four-runner nursery over this C&D (soft); creditable Listed fourth in France (1m, soft) in September but returns to a handicap off a mark 13lb higher than for his course win; further improvement needed.

runners.comment: Reappearance win came in small field but the form has been franked by the clear runner-up
runners.spotlight: Didn't really kick on last year after winning at Ascot (7f, good to firm) on debut but he reappeared at Wolverhampton (8.6f, AW) last month having been gelded and defied a slow start to win by half a length; it was a small field but the clear runner-up finished second in a good handicap at Newmarket subsequently and this fellow may well be in the mix up 6lb.

quotes.race: Juddmonte British EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (Bands A/B/C/D) (EBF Restricted Qualifier) (GBB)
quotes.quote: Hugo thought Laureate Crown was going to need the run but said he liked him a lot. You wouldn't have wanted to hear my language two furlongs out but he looks even nicer than we thought he was after that. As long as he comes out of it well, he'll go for the Group 2 Vintage Stakes [over 7f] at Goodwood. The Hays love Goodwood and will have a huge team, including the likes of Twisting Physics and Purosangue - Alex Cole, racing manager.

stable_tour.quote: He's a nice horse. He won well on his debut and then we probably overfaced him a bit. He's been gelded since his last run and he'll improve given time because he's a very big horse. 08-10-25

runners.comment: Best 2yo form came on AW but did it easily last time and he's not discounted back on turf
runners.spotlight: Improved upon first two runs (both on turf) to win at Southwell (7f, AW) last October, and followed up on handicap debut there (1m, AW); had just three rivals to beat last time and he's 12lb higher today with something to prove on turf, but is not discounted given the ease of that last win.

runners.comment: 2-2, cosily as favourite each time; Ryan Moore booked; has potential off opening mark
runners.spotlight: Well-backed winner at Ayr (7f, soft) last September on sole 2yo start and made it 2-2 in Wolverhampton novice (8.6f, AW) last month, again doing it cosily; has potential off his opening mark and the booking of Ryan Moore is a bonus.

runners.comment: Narrow win in small field on handicap debut; in good hands to continue to progress
runners.spotlight: All four starts on AW; won at Kempton (7f) in January on third run and narrowly followed up in four-runner handicap at Southwell (1m); further improvement is necessary but he's in good hands to continue to progress.

racecards.verdict: Organise is a leading contender for the Gosdens but NOBODY KNOWS also arrives 2-2 and is preferred.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/10 Organise, 11/4 Nobody Knows, 13/2 Look To The Stars, 7/1 Laureate Crown, 12/1 Capall Rasa, 20/1 Goodwood Galaxy, 33/1 Suspended Sentence

racecards.race_name: bet365 Gordon Richards Stakes (Group 3)

runners.comment: Record is 3-5; progressive before latest start (Champion Stakes); top on the figures
runners.spotlight: Record is 3-5; has gained all wins, including two Listed races, in his starts on softer than good but may yet show that he's fully effective on faster ground; drops back in class having been comfortably held in the Champion Stakes; top on the figures and he was progressive before that latest start.

quotes.race: bet365 Feilden Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Almeric is a smart horse. He's not in the Derby, but he's in the French Derby and a host of others. I think the plan would be to go to the Dante before a crack at the Prix du Jockey Club - Andrew Balding, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Racing Club EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: That was good. Almeric did well at Sandown on his debut and his pedigree suggests he's only going to get better as a three-year-old and on better ground too - P J McDonald, jockey.

runners.comment: Verging on Group class and has possibilities with usual cheekpieces reapplied
runners.spotlight: Highlight last season was a very useful performance in 1m2f handicap at Doncaster, suggesting he's verging on Group class; creditable second, despite usual cheekpieces being removed, in AW Listed event at Kempton on reappearance; possibilities with the headgear back on.

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
runners.comment: Group 3 winner for Richard Hannon in most recent domestic start; respected
runners.spotlight: Formerly trained by Richard Hannon but remained with same owner; produced his best performance in most recent domestic start, namely a narrow success in Group 3 at last year's Ebor festival at York (1m1f, good to firm); may have more to offer this term; respected.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Strensall Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: It's a win and you're in for Bahrain and King Of Cities a horse that will travel. He's very much a horse who is all about next year, though. I'll talk to Sheikh Mohammed Obaid and see what he thinks, but he was adamant about stepping this horse up in trip and was right. He's a good horse. He's nearly won a lot of nice races and just looked a bit flat-footed in the Sir Henry Cecil Stakes at Newmarket. I wish we made more use of him that day and at Goodwood, but he's a work in progress - Richard Hannon, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: An interesting recruit with a high level of form, having won a Group 3. We've not quite worked out what he wants, how good he is and where he'll start yet. He's Inisherin's half-brother and is a nice horse. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Progressive until last outing when not disgraced; C&D winner; remains of major interest
runners.spotlight: Beaten favourite in Listed race at Goodwood on last appearance but was far from disgraced, especially as he could have done with a stronger pace; progressive otherwise and landed a notable handicap at Newbury (good to firm) prior to following up over C&D (soft); remains of major interest.

quotes.race: Read Meg Nicholls' Blog At betmgm.co.uk Handicap
quotes.quote: I've always really liked Saddadd is a beautiful animal, lovely to look at, and my five-year-old girl could take him down to the start - he's so relaxed. We always thought he wanted some dig in the ground. He's genuine and an exciting horse. I think he was trying to give it all but he was still learning on the way round, finding his balance around the bend on the soft ground. He's picked up well and I think on more suitable ground with a bit of dig, you'll see a better horse. It was an impressive win carrying a lot of weight - Ray Dawson, rider.

quotes.race: Trade Nation London Gold Cup Handicap (Heritage Handicap) (GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Saddadd is a very laid back horse with a big heart. I think he'll keep improving but I do think he'll appreciate a bit more give in the ground when it comes. He's shown a lot of grit today. This race has a great history of producing Pattern performers and he might deserve a crack at something like the Hampton Court - Roger Varian, trainer.

quotes.race: Boost Your Acca At BetMGM EBF Novice Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: It was a lovely performance. I thought Saddadd would be a bit green early on, which he was jumping out and finding his stride, but I got into a nice rhythm, a nice sort of pocket to teach him a bit about having horses either side of him. He took a little bit of winding up, but once he did get into top gear, and I had the rail to just help me out a bit, the penny started to drop late on and he finished off good - Jack Mitchell, jockey, speaking to Sky Sports Racing.

stable_tour.quote: I really like him and he's a horse I expect to find a new level this season. I've got a feeling his best trip is going to be a mile and a half, and I'd quite like to start him off in the John Porter. The other option is to wait for the Gordon Richards. He prefers some cut in the ground and he's got every chance of being a good horse. We looked after him last season and he's got the physical stamp of a horse who should improve with age. 01-04-26

He's thriving and we're really happy with him. We're going to run him in the Foundation Stakes at Goodwood on Wednesday and that'll give us a guide as to what to do with him for the rest of the year. I've always loved him and I think in time he could be top drawer. He's got a great attitude. I think he's got the temperament for a good horse and he has the ability. He's my trainer's pick. 24-09-25

runners.comment: Ran well at Kempton on reappearance but isn't sure to progress further back on turf
runners.spotlight: Has gained both wins on AW and she did well to finish third, in difficult circumstances, at Kempton (1m2f Listed) on reappearance; ties in with Devil's Advocate on that bare form but isn't guaranteed to find the required further improvement back on turf.

racecards.verdict: Almeric holds leading claims, assuming the ground is okay, but KING OF CITIES and Saddadd are interesting challengers.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/4 Almeric, 3/1 King Of Cities, 7/2 Devil's Advocate, 4/1 Saddadd, 25/1 Muddy Mooy

racecards.race_name: bet365 Mile (Group 2)

runners.comment: Needs to prove he can back up the form of his 100-1 win in the Group 1 QEII
runners.spotlight: Dual C&D winner who finished third in this race last year; returns to Sandown but may be flattered by his new rating, having been perhaps helped by the draw when registering a 100-1 success in the Group 1 QEII at Ascot (good) on last appearance; needs to prove he can back up that form.

quotes.race: Queen Elizabeth II Stakes (Sponsored By Qipco) (Group 1)
quotes.quote: It's amazing. I'm speechless to be honest with you. I'm chuffed for Jason [Watson] and the owners have been brilliant. It's been so dry leading up to today and we were hoping for some rain but that obviously didn't come. It's been a tough year for us all at home. Cicero's Gift is talented but he's been a challenge; he's not been the soundest - Charlie Hills, trainer.Cicero's Gift came into this so well. I worked him the other day and was very happy with him. I'm telling you now, on the way here I just felt like something was a bit different - Jason Watson, jockey.

quotes.race: Sporting Times Sri Lanka Fortune Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: They went hard and I'm delighted with how well Cicero's Gift saw it out. We've been very patient with him this summer and it's been frustrating having to wait all those months of the season but we've always had the QEII in our minds as it can often be heavy going there. Back in the spring he wasn't beaten far here by horses like Dancing Gemini. He's got the form, he's been as sound as a pound this season and hopefully his owners' patience can be rewarded - Charles Hills, trainer.

quotes.race: Coral Challenge (Handicap)
quotes.quote: To go and win today is testament to the horse as Cicero's Gift wasn't fully wound up. The soft ground is important to him as he had bone bruising on all four fetlocks last year. We have a bit of money in the pot now so we may have to supplement him for something - Charles Hills, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He's been off since the St James's Palace Stakes with a joint problem, but he's done well and is sound now - he's been trotting for the last few weeks and looks great. He's got a lovely mind and this time last year we were really excited about him - he's very talented. He probably won't run until June or July and we'll start in a conditions race over a mile, if one exists. 17-04-24

He was one of the talking horses going into Royal Ascot after winning his first three starts. He isn't very exuberant at home and when you watch him he does nothing flashy. He's so laid back and just does what you ask. We had him out nice and early this year and he won a Wolverhampton novice on his return. That was pretty much what we expected and he then went to Goodwood for a strong conditions race over a mile, which he won very nicely again. On the back of those wins we went for the St James's Palace on Tuesday, although he could only manage seventh on the day behind Paddington. He's a strong, athletic type like his dad, but a little bigger than him. It's an unusual route to this race but on what he's done it was the next logical step. He's clearly effective over a mile but I think he should get 1m2f later on. 21-06-23

runners.comment: Group 1 winner at Meydan last time; no match for Zeus Olympios in last domestic start
runners.spotlight: Progressive colt who readily bagged Group 1 honours at Meydan (1m1f, good) three months ago, taking record to 6-8; however, appears to need further improvement to defy 5lb penalty and was no match for Zeus Olympios in last domestic outing.

quotes.race: Jebel Hatta Presented By Longines (Group 1) (Turf)
quotes.quote: We felt that we have a good horse on our hands for some time now. Opera Ballo was still a bit headstrong in the first quarter mile but, like William [Buick] says, they just can't go fast enough for him. He doesn't take a lot of training but he's got his Group one and he's a horse who is exciting going forward - Charlie Appleby, trainer, speaking to Racing Dubai.

quotes.race: Al Rashidiya Sponsored By Emaar (Group 2) (Turf)
quotes.quote: The race set up a little bit better for Opera Ballo, he had cover which was crucial, stepping up a furlong in trip. We were wanting to learn something tonight, and we wanted to teach him something as well. We always thought he was a horse worthy of going to the top level at some stage, and he showed tonight he's on his way there - William Buick, jockey, speaking on Racing Dubai TV.

quotes.race: Edmondson Hall Solicitors Sir Henry Cecil Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: We would have been disappointed if Opera Ballo hadn't won today to be honest. He has a proper engine, it's just a case of getting it to go in the right direction. We'll be taking baby steps with him but he's a horse for next year possibly over a mile and a quarter. There's a race at Deauville we could look at - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

quotes.race: Star Sports Heron Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Opera Ballo settled much better than at Newmarket last time and it's good to see him get it done. He's very much a work in progress, the hood has helped a lot. I'm not quite sure what Charlie has planned but he appreciated a bit of juice in the ground and I wouldn't say Royal Ascot is a definite at this stage - Alex Merriam, assistant trainer.

quotes.race: "European Road To The Kentucky Derby" Conditions Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Opera Ballo was very smooth. I was very pleased with him. I do think he's a work in progress, but it's all there for him - William Buick, jockey, speaking on Racing TV.

quotes.race: Unibet Supports Safer Gambling Maiden Stakes (GBB Race) (Div I)
quotes.quote: Opera Ballo is a beautiful horse. Just watching him going around the paddock was nice and he really impressed me with the way he went about his business. He was very professional. He jumped with the blind, but he got away lovely and I managed to find a nice slot. He was still actually quite green, he overraced a little bit, and he'll probably be better with a little bit of cover going forward, but from the gate it was all about getting him out and into a rhythm. When I asked him to stretch at the two pole, he lengthened away quite quickly and gave me a nice feel. I think another run with experience would definitely benefit him, especially if the option was there to get a mile on some turf. I think it would help getting him to switch off early ? we've seen his finishing kick ? and it could enhance that - Billy Loughnane, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.owner: Exors Of The Late Sheikh Mohammed Obaid
runners.comment: Highly progressive in his first season and still unbeaten (4-4); remains one to follow
runners.spotlight: Highly progressive in his first campaign last year and still unbeaten (4-4); won going away from Opera Ballo in Group 2 at Newmarket (1m, good to firm) on final start; remains one to follow and has the makings of a Group 1 colt this term; commands respect.

quotes.race: BOYLE Sports Daily Racing Rewards Joel Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: Zeus Olympios is a lovely horse, a great-natured horse who goes about his work really well and all he's done is physically improve from month to month at home. I thought it [step up to Group 2] might be a little step too far at this stage but it was the last race he could run in and that's shown us exactly where we're going next year. I'd imagine we'd start off in the Lockinge [next season] and that will tell us whether we're staying at a mile or stepping up but he's obviously a horse with a big turn of foot - Karl Burke, trainer.We've liked Zeus Olympios ever since he came to the yard. We had heard a lot about him and that he was a very good horse and with every run he's had he's improved a hell of a lot. He is very tall and I think next year he will fill out a bit stronger. He is a lovely horse with a great attitude. He stayed the trip very well and saw it out nicely so he could step up in trip but at the same time he has plenty of boot underneath him. Flight Plan has got plenty of boot so he was the pace. I had William Buick and Colin Keane upsides me and they just tried to box seat me a little but I made sure I was on the ball - Clifford Lee, jockey.

quotes.race: Best Odds On The Betfair Exchange Superior Mile Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: I thought it was a very good performance. Zeus Olympios has a great mind and took everything in his stride. William [Buick] said as soon as he jumped and went a furlong, he knew he was sat on a good horse. I was a bit worried whether I was doing the right thing dropping him into this grade, but there's a lack of black type races over this trip. He's only going to improve. I'll speak to Sheikh Mohammed Obaid but I don't really want to throw him in too deep this time round. Next year will be his year - Karl Burke, trainer.

quotes.race: Weekly Money Back Races At Unibet Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: Zeus Olympios has been working really well at home but he's had his niggles. He's done that quite nicely in a race that didn't feel that strong. I thought going to the 2f pole I was going to pick them up and do it quite easily, but then the greenness kicked in and I had to get after him. He'll be even better, probably over a mile, next time - Clifford Lee, jockey, talking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: A very exciting horse, it's just a shame Sheikh Mohammed Obaid isn't around to see him. Hopefully, he turns out as good as we've hoped. He's very straightforward and has a high cruising speed and a turn of foot. We could go straight to the Lockinge or we could take in the Sandown Mile as a prep run. He'd have a penalty but he's more than capable of handling that. He's very forward, is working nicely and is fit. Newbury and the Queen Anne are the key early targets. 31-03-26

runners.comment: Won this race last year but is facing a slightly stiffer assignment in this field
runners.spotlight: Below best in three of his last four outings in 2025 but commenced the campaign splendidly, winning twice (including in this race) then going close in the Group 1 Lockinge; while today may be a good time to catch him, he faces a slightly stiffer assignment in this field.

quotes.race: BoyleSports Lockinge Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: Dancing Gemini has run a cracker but that ground was rattling fast. I asked the clerk of the course on Friday if he'd put a bit of water on it Friday but he wasn't playing ball."That's quicker ground than he's ever been on, but we've only gone down a neck. We don't duck and dive and will go to Ascot next. He went down on his sword and is a Group 1 winner waiting to happen - Roger Teal, trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Mile (Group 2)
quotes.quote: We always thought Dancing Gemini could do what he has done today and that is why we were pitching him in all the Group races last year. Unfortunately, it was such a wet summer last year and we never got a chance. Everyone kept labelling him a soft ground horse but he's not a soft ground horse. I was delighted to see him win like that again today. I know some of the field will improve for today but Mr Fabre's horse was fit and he's no mug - he was third behind us in the French Guineas when we were runner-up. Haatem is also a serious horse. The Lockinge and the Prix d'Ispahan are the options now. We've got to get him a Group 1 and we'll do what is best for him so it's not decided yet. We'll see how the dust settles after today - Roger Teal, trainer.

quotes.race: William Hill Doncaster Mile Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: Dancing Gemini likes this track! I'm absolutely delighted. We've always had high hopes for this horse, doing what he did there in a quality field I'm very excited. We thought we'd start at a mile. He's bred for further and he's got that blistering turn of foot - sometimes if it's not broken don't fix it. We've got some talking to do now because there's the Group Two at Sandown he could go to but he could just go straight to Newbury - and it's local! - Roger Teal, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfred Derby (Group 1) (British Champions Series) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: Dancing Gemini ran well. I rode him to finish and he just emptied out. He'll be better back in trip - Dylan Browne McMonagle, rider.

quotes.race: Emirates Poule d'Essai des Poulains (Group 1) (3yo Colts) (Grande Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: We'll let the dust settle and then we'll have a discussion. Whether Dancing Gemini will stay a mile and a half around Epsom or maybe do you come back here over a mile and a quarter - there's lots to discuss. He's always had that kick and maybe he might have too much speed for a mile and a half, and coming here might be the wise thing. He'll have come on for today and he's had no prep - Roger Teal, trainer.

quotes.race: Betfred Flying Scotsman Stakes (Listed Race)
quotes.quote: That was really impressive. We've held Dancing Gemini in high regard all year and he did a piece of work last week that was breathtaking. I knew we had him in good shape coming into today and I said to Lewis if he can back up that bit of work you'll be going pass that lollipop in front. It was a very nice performance. We won this with Tip Two Win and he could possibly be as good. He's got a similar profile, he's got speed, he's got a turn of foot and he's got a good cruising gear. He's in the Futurity here but we'll play it by ear, we'll see how he comes out of today. If all's well and the owner is happy we might take a punt on it. If not we'll leave him for next year, maybe do a trial and go on to the Guineas - Roger Teal, trainer.

quotes.race: Chapel Down British EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB/IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: Dancing Gemini in probably one of the nicest two-year-olds already. We don't get many but we know when we've got a good horse and I've got a lot of butterflies about this horse. He's still a tad green but he went away nicely and he was very professional - Roger Teal, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: He did a nice piece of work last Wednesday and it's all systems go now. He won't be doing anything too special between now and the race, just some healthy exercises. He's fit and he's ready, and we just want to keep him ticking over. He did us proud in the Lockinge when just pipped by Lead Artist so hopefully he can put in a similar performance.  10-06-25

runners.comment: Impressive in Irish 2,000 Guineas and SJP prior to excusable defeats; sets the standard
runners.spotlight: Very progressive until having plausible excuses in the Sussex Stakes (found to be lame) and QEII (draw to some extent) in last two appearances; impressive wins in the Irish 2,000 Guineas and St James's Palace Stakes make him the one to beat, provided he's back in similar form.

quotes.race: Queen Elizabeth II Stakes (Sponsored By Qipco) (Group 1)
quotes.quote: Field Of Gold has run a very good race. He came into it well but the lack of a recent race just caught him out in the final furlong. He's had a long time off and was having a good blow afterwards. He's worked well at home but it's nothing like coming here with a prep race. I didn't like the high draw. It wasn't ideal and he was always on the wing, rather than in amongst it where the pace was on the other side, but it's a lack of a recent race that has caught him out, a lack of match practice. He's a huge striding horse and I don't think he'd necessarily want to tackle two bends at Del Mar [in the Breeders' Cup Mile] - John Gosden, joint-trainer.Field Of Gold relaxed and travelled through the race well. Coming down to the two it felt like he was picking up to be competitive, but a lack of a run cost us. He's run a massive race after being off for so long - Colin Keane, jockey.

quotes.race: Visit Qatar Sussex Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: We got left back a long way, that's life, and the pacemaker goes and wins it. If you let them have those fractions they'll do it. Field Of Gold ran on but didn't seem well balanced on the track. It's a different kind of track than he's run on and he just got a little imbalanced coming out of the dip into the bend but I'm not making any excuses. He ran a huge race in the Guineas and was flying at the finish. He was not flying at the finish here so it was very different. We'll have to see why [he wasn't at his best]. He's having a normal blow and we'll have a good look. He didn't seem comfortable and William said as soon as he asked him, the engine wasn't there, simple as that. And if not, he'd have run on and probably been with Rosallion in second or right up there but he didn't fire today - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: St James's Palace Stakes (Group 1) (Colts)
quotes.quote: That was a great performance. Field Of Gold had always impressed as a two-year-old, but he was a big boy and slightly outgrew himself. It was never the plan to go to Ireland, it became the plan, so he's had a trial, two Guineas and this. It's a lot of racing and we're not even beginning to be half-way through the season. Maybe freshen and go to the Sussex, something like that, we'll see. I think if he hadn't have run in Ireland, I would have probably been keen to go to the Eclipse - John Gosden, joint-trainer.I thought we'd be behind Will [Buick] and Ryan [Moore] would be behind us, whereabouts I wasn't sure exactly but it worked out to some degree and he showed how good he is on the day. I had a lot of confidence in Field Of Gold but I needed them to have brought him a little bit further because he'll only do so much when he gets there. I didn't want to land there and be a sitting duck for something to come at me so If I asked him I thought they'd do well to catch him - Colin Keane, jockey.

quotes.race: Tattersalls Irish 2,000 Guineas (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: I was sorry to get beaten in the 2,000 Guineas when Field Of Gold finished so well, but to come on a plane and see something different, he'll have learned a lot, and they grow in mentality and in stature. Colin [Keane] rode him beautifully. In truth, I was concerned he might over-race with no cover on the outside, but I told Colin if he relaxes on the way down [to the start], he should relax on the way back. When he quickened he went, and it took two or three strides and he was off. Let's hope the owners want to go to Ascot and have a look at the St James's Palace Stakes - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Betfred 2000 Guineas Stakes (Group 1) (No Geldings)
quotes.quote: The race wasn't probably run in the fractions of the Craven Stakes and we were sat some way back. The winner has kicked and gone and we ran out of racetrack. Given another 25 yards the race would have been ours.    You'll probably find Field Of Gold has run a better race than he did in the trial but a trial is a trial. When this track gets fast like this it can ride slick with a crosstail wind and they can get away from you. It just got away from us, I'm afraid, as we came into the Dip from where he was clawing the ground back. I could see it was lost going into the Dip as we were just too far back and the winner got first run. We'll talk with the family about where we go next but I think you're looking at a St James's Palace Stakes after that - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: bet365 Craven Stakes (Group 3) (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: This is a trial, it's not the Guineas. You're not fully wound up for this, the race now puts them where you want them - that's the idea of the trial. He went to his girth and had a good blow, but then he's entitled to. Field Of Gold did it in splendid style and it's nice to race on some really good ground today and he just flew off it. It would be nice to win, but it's not something you necessarily worry about - I don't think about it at all. I suppose Kingman was slightly unfortunate as he went four lengths clear and thought he'd done enough and got caught late on by a very good horse in Night Of Thunder, who has become a top stallion. It's lovely to have a horse going for the Guineas and it's great for Juddmonte, because they have both the winner of the Greenham and this, so they're double-handed if they want to. But the family will decide whether one goes there and one goes to France or what we do - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Qatar Prix Jean-Luc Lagardere (Group 1) (2yo Colts & Fillies) (New Course) (Turf)
quotes.quote: Fields Of Gold ran a solid race. He was right up there and travelled well but got a little bit caught out by the ground. He's a big, strapping horse and very much a next-year horse - John Gosden, joint-trainer.

quotes.race: Sky Bet Solario Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Field Of Gold is very exciting. He's always shown great potential at home and it's nice to see him finally deliver it on the track. He's a horse who will stay a mile but he has acceleration and a very good turn of foot. He's a big horse - 16 hands - and is going to be better as he strengthens and will hopefully make a better three-year-old. The Lagardère looks the obvious plan at this stage - Barry Mahon, Juddmonte racing manager.

quotes.race: Weatherbys British EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Field Of Gold has taken a big step forward, albeit he probably ran in a nice race at Doncaster. He was slowly away that day but he was quick today and I was just trying to get a lead for as long as I could. We hit the front a long way out but he knew his job today and he's got a huge stride and plenty of scope. He really galloped out and he's no doubt going to stay a mile - Kieran Shoemark, jockey.

runners.comment: Did very well last season for new yard; not disgraced in QEII; may rate higher still
runners.spotlight: Did very well (3-5) last season for new stable, completing a notable summer hat-trick (7f/1m, good to firm) that culminated in Group 1 success at York; not disgraced from unfavourable draw in the QEII on final outing; may rate higher still and looks likely to go well.

quotes.race: Sky Bet City Of York Stakes (Group 1)
quotes.quote: Never So Brave has kept on improving. To win over seven furlongs then to win over a mile then drop back to seven again shows he's pretty versatile. He's probably got an exciting campaign ahead. He did it pretty well today but Oisin said that he felt that a mile is probably going to be the better spot for him - Anna Lisa Balding.

quotes.race: Cornish Orchards Summer Mile Stakes (Group 2)
quotes.quote: I was confident enough because if Never So Brave was relaxed he was good enough to be winning. He's very good and I'm thrilled with his progression. We put him in the Lennox but he's versatile in terms of trip from six furlongs to a mile. I don't know where he goes, this opens up a few options as he showed he gets a mile - Andrew Balding, trainer.I reverted to plan B. I didn't know what the pace would turn out to be but it turned out to be quite strong and Jamie [Spencer, on Point Lynas] slipped us and was ten lengths ahead turning into the straight. Luckily I had a real reliable companion underneath me and Never So Brave filled me with confidence. He quickened so well and even a furlong and a half out I felt I'd go away and win. He's quite talented but it's difficult for a horse to come out of a handicap and into a Group race like he's done but he's improved leaps and bounds through the winter and since Andrew [Balding, trainer] has got him. He's an exciting horse. To ride such a good winner like this is a privilege - David Probert, jockey.

quotes.race: Buckingham Palace Stakes (Handicap)
quotes.quote: Never So Brave was gelded over the winter which may have helped him, but I know Sir Michael [Stoute] always had a high opinion of him - he ran him in the Jersey Stakes last year - and he was probably a Group horse in a handicap today. He settled well today, and I think the key to him is to try to get him to relax at an early stage of the race. He's got an excellent turn of foot if he can do that. He has been easy to train - the guys at home have done a brilliant job with him because he's not a very patient horse, he wants to get up the gallops first and get his exercise done, and they've done a lovely job with him. I'm really thrilled - Andrew Balding, trainer.Never So Brave was very good. His work has been excellent. I was worried he might get stuck in traffic from that draw, but he didn't, and I deliberately started a bit further back to allow the race to happen in front of him. If anything he got there very easily. He's a four-year-old now and I'd hope he will step up to Pattern company - Oisin Murphy, jockey.

quotes.race: Halliwell Jones Handicap
quotes.quote: Never So Brave showed some nice form last year and he's come out this year and practically won as he liked at Thirsk. He's just kept progressing and this was a step up to find out whether we're still going in the right direction and he's done everything he was asked to do. It's difficult to say how high he'll go but he did that quite nicely and if he got the mile, you'd like to think he'd be a Britannia horse - Philip Robinson, racing manager to Saeed Suhail, owner.

racecards.verdict: Field Of Gold sets a tall standard assuming he's back in top form. ZEUS OLYMPIOS is still unbeaten and still on the up.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/10 Field Of Gold, 9/4 Zeus Olympios, 13/2 Never So Brave, 8/1 Opera Ballo, 12/1 Dancing Gemini, 20/1 Cicero's Gift

racecards.race_name: bet365 Classic Trial (Group 3)

runners.owner: Michael Tabor & Derrick Smith & Mrs John Magnier
runners.comment: Ended progressive 2yo campaign with close second in the Group 1 Futurity; the form pick
runners.spotlight: Closely related to last year's Derby winner Lambourn and has his own Epsom aspirations, having ended a progressive 2yo campaign with close second to one of his stablemates in the Group 1 Futurity at Doncaster (1m, heavy); now goes in tongue-tie; the pick on the figures and may well rate higher still.

quotes.race: Whiriskey Refrigeration Irish EBF Maiden
quotes.quote: Action is quite a big horse, he stays well and ideally I would have loved to have gone a stride quicker but he was having such a look in front I was letting him find his feet and get comfortable. I thought the last 50 yards he hit the line well. He is going to learn plenty from today - Wayne Lordan, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

stable_tour.quote: He ran a very good race in the Futurity Trophy when second to Hawk Mountain and he'll be trained for a Derby. I'd imagine it'll be Epsom as he looks an Epsom type. He'll run in a trial, probably at Chester or Leopardstown. 31-03-26

runners.comment: AW Group 3 win in France took his record to 2-3; further progress may materialise
runners.spotlight: Dubawi colt who got up in the final strides to win 1m1f AW Group 3 at Chantilly on final 2yo start, taking record to 2-3; looks likely to be well suited by going up further in distance; doesn't have a Derby entry but further progress may materialise.

quotes.race: Emirates Autumn Stakes (Group 3)
quotes.quote: Al Zanati is hard to teach as he would never do that at home, but he has another run under his belt and that should man him up - Charlie Appleby, trainer.

runners.comment: Clear peak form when running well in the Solario; won French Group 3 next time
runners.spotlight: Narrowly bagged Group 3 honours at Chantilly (1m, soft) in September when last seen but still needs to prove he can repeat the clear peak form he appeared to show when going close at 25-1 in an exciting Solario at Sandown; gelding who has no major entries in the future.

quotes.race: Prix des Chenes - Fonds Europeen de l'Elevage (Group 3) (2yo Colts & Geldings) (Turf)
quotes.quote: This was the right race for Oceans Four after the Solario and I didn't want to go to Newmarket with him next week, so it made sense to supplement him here. There's a possibility we'll consider the Breeders' Cup Juvenile Turf at Del Mar. That was one of the reasons for bringing him here for the Group 3, because he needed to win a stakes race to guarantee a spot. He's a gelding so there's quite a few races he doesn't qualify for, but that makes things less complicated. He's a lovely horse who I think the world of and he keeps improving. He improved again today and he had to quicken off a slow pace, while from what I heard beforehand, we beat some very nice two-year-olds - Brian Meehan, trainer.

runners.comment: Smartly bred; justified favouritism at Ascot in sole 2yo outing; bright prospect
runners.spotlight: Smartly bred, being a brother to Baaeed and Hukum; duly showed strong promise in justifying favouritism at Ascot (7f, soft) in sole 2yo outing; held a Royal Lodge entry at the time and currently holds three major entries, including the Derby; should be suited by middle distances; bright prospect.

quotes.race: Charbonnel et Walker British EBF Maiden Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: He's got a very laid-back attitude and I thought from that draw in stall 1 Raaheeb was very professional. He got a lot of cover but he travelled well and went through the race very pleasingly. Nothing's going to quicken in this ground too much because Jim [Crowley] said it's pretty soft, but he lengthened and went up through and hit the line strongly. He's a miler now, and I think he'll be a mile-and-a-quarter, mile-and-a-half horse next year. He's only been on the grass once but he's done everything pleasingly at home, with a very laid-back attitude. Once he switches on he'll be better, Jim said going under the tunnel there he tripped twice because he was half asleep, but that's a good way to have them at this stage. We'll see how he comes out of it. Whatever we can get from him this year is just going to be a bonus, so we won't go too mad - Owen Burrows, trainer.The Royal Lodge would be straight into deeper territory. I'd have loved to have gone for the Haynes, Hanson & Clark Stakes but that's even quicker and that's a no-no. There's possibly the Somerville Tattersall Stakes [on September 25] but we'll just go gently with Raaheeb. He's a big, raw horse and it's more about the future. It's just lovely to see he's got the ability to do that first time - Angus Gold, Shadwell racing manager.

runners.comment: Developing into a useful Flat performer for his esteemed dual-purpose trainer
runners.spotlight: Eye-catching second in the Convivial Maiden at York then went one better at Yarmouth and ran well in Group 3 at Newmarket (1m2f, good to firm) upped further in trip; developing into a useful Flat performer for his esteemed dual-purpose trainer.

quotes.race: British Stallion Studs EBF 'Confined' Maiden Stakes (No More Than Three Runs) (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: I'm delighted with Spyce. The closer I got to the race, the more I thought it was seriously hot. And it was. The front two have pulled a long way clear, and he will have learnt plenty from that. He's only been on grass twice before today and that was at the breeze-up sales and when he ran at York, as we haven't been able to get them out on it at home. He's got an entry in the Futurity Trophy, but let's just see how he comes out of this at home - Alan King, trainer.

runners.comment: AW form comprises a win and good second; faces a stiffer task at this level
runners.spotlight: Both starts on AW, scoring comfortably at Southwell (7f) as a 2yo then running well under a penalty at Kempton (1m); holds a Derby entry and may be suited by going up further in distance today but faces a stiff task at this level; bottom on bare figures.

runners.comment: Scored comfortably at Nottingham, looking the type who could become a Group colt
runners.spotlight: Ghaiyyath colt whose two major entries include the Derby; scored comfortably at Nottingham (1m, good to soft) in sole 2yo start, looking the type who'll be suited by middle distances and could develop into a Group performer this year; interesting contender.

racecards.verdict: Big potential is brought by RAAHEEB and Wise Prince, while Action sets the standard and isn't opposed with absolute confidence.
racecards.betting_forecast: 6/4 Action, 5/2 Wise Prince, 7/2 Raaheeb, 9/1 Al Zanati, 14/1 Spyce, 20/1 Oceans Four, 33/1 Winding Stream

racecards.race_name: bet365 "Wild Card" Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners.comment: Oaks entry who won well at Lingfield (AW) in sole 2yo start; open to progress
runners.spotlight: Oaks entry who won well at Lingfield (1m, AW) in sole 2yo start and looks open to progress this term; faces fairly deep opposition but defying a 6lb penalty is not out of the question.

quotes.race: Bet £10 Get £40 With BetMGM Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
quotes.quote: We're thrilled. Felicitas will be better for going further next year, but we're very impressed. We expected her to run well, but perhaps not quite that emphatically on debut. She's an exciting filly, and we'll see where we start her in the spring. We'll see how she's working, as she's a big filly with lots of scope and is very exciting for next year - Ed Walker, trainer.

stable_tour.quote: She's very exciting and will have an Oaks campaign, whether it be Epsom or Chantilly - I'm not convinced she'll stay 1m4f. She's done well physically and could start in a fillies' novice at Sandown or the Pretty Polly Stakes at Newmarket. We've always thought a lot of her. We were pleased with her winning debut at Lingfield and we've been happy with her this spring. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Scored at Wolverhampton on reappearance and is the type to rate higher still
runners.spotlight: Justified favouritism at Wolverhampton (9.5f, AW) on reappearance and is the type to rate higher still, being a Sea The Stars filly who cost 1,600,000gns as a yearling; respected.

runners.comment: Debutante by Study Of Man out of Listed winner for her connections; interesting
runners.spotlight: Debutante by Study Of Man out of a 1m2f winner (including Listed; RPR 105) for her connections; interesting, especially if the market speaks favourably.

runners.comment: Fared better upped to 1m2f in latest Yarmouth start; Oaks entry; possibilities
runners.spotlight: Dubawi filly who cost 925,000gns as a yearling and holds an Oaks entry; both starts at Yarmouth, better effort when third upped to 1m2f latest; possibilities with another step forward likely.

runners.comment: Bottom of this pack judged on her 2yo effort at Newbury
runners.spotlight: May do better in due course but is perhaps one for handicaps later on; bottom of this pack judged on her 2yo effort at Newbury (1m, soft).

stable_tour.quote: She would have made her debut in the same fillies' maiden at Goodwood as Brighlee if we'd had a significant amount of rain. She's a well-bred filly, being by No Nay Never out of a Camelot dam who's related to Harzand. She's shown some good things on the gallops but I want to see some ease in the ground for her. 30-07-25

runners.comment: Oaks entry; plenty of promise at Yarmouth, beating all bar the market leader
runners.spotlight: Oaks entry who showed plenty of promise at Yarmouth (1m, good to soft) six months ago, beating all bar the market leader and faring best of the newcomers; enters the reckoning.

runners.comment: 70,000gns yearling; by Space Blues out of German Oaks winner
runners.spotlight: 70,000gns yearling; Space Blues half-sister to five winners, notably California Dreamer (1m AW; Irish 1,000 Guineas runner-up; RPR 110); dam German Oaks winner; check the betting.

runners.comment: Something to find on her October efforts but remains open to improvement
runners.spotlight: Something to find on her October efforts (1m) but remains open to improvement, being an Oaks entry who is related to several winners for her owner-breeder.

runners.comment: 110,000euros yearling; by New Bay; one of two newcomers for her stable
runners.spotlight: 110,000euros yearling; New Bay half-sister to five winners, notably Patrick Sarsfield (1m-1m2f including Group 3; RPR 114); one of two newcomers for her stable; market instructive.

runners.comment: Oaks entry; close second at Kempton in sole 2yo run; winner waiting to happen
runners.spotlight: Entered in the Oaks, which her half-sister Soul Sister won for her connections in 2023; close second and clear of remainder at Kempton (1m, AW) in sole 2yo run, faring best of the newcomers; a winner waiting to happen and her yard has a good record in this race.

racecards.verdict: The signs look particularly good for SUNSHINE STAR who is first choice ahead of similar type Ladykirk.
racecards.betting_forecast: 11/10 Sunshine Star, 5/2 Ribbon Of Sea, 5/1 Felicitas, 12/1 Bintsaleh,  Ladykirk, 14/1 Ruby Wedding, 20/1 Alma Latina, 33/1 Corallience, 40/1 Palomezcal, 50/1 Sullom Voe

racecards.race_name: Nordoff & Robbins Ozzy Osbourne Memorial Handicap

runners.comment: Returned to action with 4l win in recent Bath novice and he's respected on handicap debut
runners.spotlight: Runner-up to exciting prospect at Kempton (1m, AW) in December on third and final 2yo start and returned to action with 4l win in Bath novice (1m2f, good) this month; likeable prospect who is respected on handicap debut.

runners.comment: Promising over 1m on his three 2yo starts and bred to appreciate this longer trip
runners.spotlight: Promising third last year on first two starts (1m, good/soft) then won Haydock maiden (1m, good to soft) in September; his dam was a 1m2f/1m4f winner and it seems likely that he'll improve for this step up in trip on handicap/seasonal debut; trainer won this in 2024.

quotes.race: J&P Civil Engineering British EBF Maiden Stakes (Colts & Geldings)
quotes.quote: Lost Boys is quite big and immature and he's a May foal, so it's a bit of a miracle that he's managed to run three times this year. Everything this season has been a bonus so I'd like to think he's a nice horse in the making. It's a bit too soon to make plans for next season, but I'd imagine we'd be looking at races over ten furlongs or further. It depends on how he does over the winter, he could gain more speed. He's very straightforward and looks a nice prospect for next year - David Menuisier, trainer.

runners.comment: Godolphin colt; could prove to be on an advantageous mark for his first handicap start
runners.spotlight: Defied inexperience to win on debut at Lingfield (1m2f, AW) in February and again ran well when 3l second to a newcomer at Southwell (1m4f, AW) last month; his dam was a Listed winner and he could prove to be on an advantageous mark for his first handicap start.

quotes.race: BetMGM Supports Safer Gambling Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)
quotes.quote: Into The Light was a step slow out of the stalls and raced behind the bridle for the first few furlongs. It turned into a messy race down the back, but once I was able to get into a nice position he was always the horse to beat. As we turned in I got a lovely split up the inside and Jack [Mitchell, on Al Azd] got carried wide, but even when he came to me my lad knuckled down well. If Jack had the horse he could have come past, but my lad had that bit more class. I was expecting him to run nicely and he looks like a fun horse to have going forward - Connor Planas, rider.

runners.comment: Highly likely that he'll relish going beyond 1m for the first time; firmly in calculations
runners.spotlight: Won on debut at Bath (1m, good to soft) last September before 8l last of eight in Italian Group 3 (7.5f, good); reappeared with strong finish for third in Kempton novice (1m, AW) this month and his pedigree also suggests he'll relish the extra yardage today; firmly in calculations.

runners.comment: 0-4 last year; bred to be suited by the longer trip but needs improvement off opening mark
runners.spotlight: Best of his four 2yo runs came when second here (7f, soft) in August, and he also showed promise on fast ground; bred to be suited by the step up in trip but he was headstrong on occasions last year, which is a concern, and improvement is needed off his opening mark.

runners.comment: There's stamina in his pedigree; possible improver up in trip on this first handicap start
runners.spotlight: Took a step forward when up in trip and third at Newbury (1m, soft) last October on his third start; ran well on good ground on debut; there's stamina in his pedigree and he's a possible improver on this first handicap start.

racecards.verdict: All are open to improvement but MAGIC TRIP (nap) looks a good prospect for this sort of trip and is preferred over Lost Boy.
racecards.betting_forecast: 9/4 Lost Boys, 100/30 Into The Light,  Magic Trip, 11/2 Bnaider, 6/1 Colourband, 12/1 The Joker

racecards.race_name: Welcome To Cork Racecourse Mallow Maiden

runners.comment: 100,000euros yearling was fifth of eight at the Curragh on debut but not beaten far
runners.spotlight: Son of Wootton Bassett cost 100,000euros as a yearling; weak in the betting on debut (20-1) when fifth of eight at the Curragh (1m1f, soft to heavy) three weeks ago; beaten only 3.75l and improvement can be expected.

runners.comment: Modest fourth behind stablemate/favourite Allsortz over 6f at Dundalk; bred to stay trip
runners.spotlight: Bated Breath gelding cost 20,000euros; went modest fourth behind stablemate and favourite Allsortz over 6f on debut at Dundalk a fortnight ago; bred to appreciate the step up in trip on turf debut; in the mix.

runners.comment: Bred for the AW but didn't show a whole pile at Dundalk last year; turf debut; gelded
runners.spotlight: Bred for the AW but didn't show a whole pile on 1m Dundalk debut in October although bit better over same C&D when sixth of 14 in December; gelded; turf debut; stable in form.

runners.owner: A K Whelan & Reeves Thoroughbred Racing

prev_owners.owner: A K Whelan & Reeves Thoroughbred Racing
A K Whelan & Reeves Thoroughbred Racing

runners.comment: Posted good efforts in Group company last year; sets the standard dropping down in class
runners.spotlight: Second runner for yard; promise when fourth on debut at the Curragh; not disgraced in 1m Leopardstown Group 2 on second start; ran to similar level when beaten 6l behind smart Ballydoyle colt in 1m1f Leopardstown Group 3; fair chance with sights lowered on return; holds Irish Derby entry.

runners.comment: 8l fourth of seven on 7f Dundalk debut in December; will need to improve significantly
runners.spotlight: Palace Pier colt cost 40,000euros; backed in from big prices (sent off 10-1) when 8l fourth of seven on 7f Dundalk debut in December; will need to improve significantly to take this.

runners.comment: Triple-figure odds and never a factor on 1m Curragh debut in October; look elsewhere
runners.spotlight: Triple-figure odds and never a factor on 1m Curragh debut in October; safe to look elsewhere.

runners.comment: Close third in Listed at Tipperary last year (Brussels second) is solid form; enjoys good
runners.spotlight: Best effort a close third in Listed heat at Tipperary (7.5f, good; dual Group 1 runner-up Brussels second); poor effort next time on soft at Roscommon; gelded ahead of 7f Dundalk maiden third in October; big player on return with drying ground in his favour.

runners.breeder: His Highness The Aga Khan's Studs S C
runners.owner: Exors Of The Late H H Aga Khan
runners.comment: Two solid efforts at the Curragh; best run at Navan on latest but was on heavy; race-fit
runners.spotlight: Made encouraging Curragh debut last July, staying on late over 7f; failed to improve over same C&D following month; best effort yet when runner-up to Ballydoyle colt at Navan (1m) on return last month but that was on heavy; has race-fitness on his side.

racecards.verdict: SUSPICIOUS MINDZ is a big player judged on his Tipperary 3rd last term when right behind the classy Brussels

racecards.race_name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Median Auction Race

runners.comment: Won on track debut at Leopardstown on good; well below that on soft at Killarney; absence
runners.spotlight: Fourth in Naas barrier trial before successful track debut in 7f Leopardstown auction event (good) last summer, overcoming traffic problems to get up on post; ran below that level when beaten odds-on favourite at Killarney (1m, soft) in July; 282 days off; tongue-tied.

quotes.race: Irish EBF Auction Series Race (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: He just did it all wrong. Dial Me In stepped quite slow, he was backing off them all the way down until we got to the 4f pole and then I got a bit of room. He's probably a slow learner but has stepped forward a lot from the barrier trial, there is plenty in there. He'll sharpen up for the run - Declan McDonogh, jockey, speaking to Racing TV

runners.comment: Roscommon maiden winner on good; ran no race at Dundalk on return; this is tough
runners.spotlight: Left previous form behind when winning Roscommon maiden in August (7.5f, good), value for more as had to wait for a gap; weakened badly on AW debut at Dundalk in February; likely to come up short in this company; blinkers.

runners.comment: Won barrier trial and debut; entitled to go well and fresh may be the time to catch her
runners.spotlight: Won Naas barrier trial last May; successful track debut at Leopardstown (7f, soft) in June; failed to make a major impact in good-class contests thereafter, on latest when midfield in the Goffs Million; entitled to go well at this level and fresh may be the time to catch her.

quotes.race: Irish EBF Median Sires Series Fillies Maiden (IRE Incentive Race)
quotes.quote: I think Brownstown is a smart filly and has a bit of class, she's been doing everything right at home. She's a big, long-striding filly, picked up well from the 2f to the 1f marker, just got a bit tired inside the final furlong. Nicer ground will help her, she'll come on for that and she has the size and scope to keep improving - Gary Carroll, jockey, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Each-way player judged on Curragh third last year and possibly needed the run last month
runners.spotlight: Nondescript run at Naas on debut last September; promising third at the Curragh following month (soft to heavy; form worked out well); perhaps needed the run when below-par at the Curragh last month.

runners.comment: Won 7f Dundalk maiden in style but finished last in Listed at Lingfield; turf debut
runners.spotlight: Promise in two Dundalk runs for Cormac Farrell; impressive winning debut for this yard at Dundalk (7f) in February; finished last of eight when pitched into Listed company at Lingfield on latest; turf debut.

quotes.race: Irishinjuredjockeys.com Fillies Maiden
quotes.quote: We thought Star Strewn would win the first night she ran here but she was just a little bit weak, but she's straightened up really well now. I definitely think she's a black-type filly - there's no doubt. We'll put her away and bring her back for the turf later on, we don't want to go handicapping as she's better than that. It's great to have a filly like this. She's going to strengthen up really well, and we might even talk about a Guineas trial later on in the year - Adrian McGuinness, trainer, speaking to Racing TV.

runners.comment: Clearly highly thought of as yet to run outside of Group company; bred to get a mile
runners.spotlight: Belied 40-1 odds with strong-finishing second in Curragh Group 3 (6f, good to yielding) where he was the sole newcomer in the field; inexperience costly when in rear in the Middle Park; slowly away when respectable fifth in Leopardstown Group 3 on return 12 days ago; bred to get the mile and could be a class apart.

stable_tour.quote: He ran very well when fifth at Leopardstown when it was hard to make up any ground. He'll probably go to Cork this month and I think he can make it into Group company this season over 7f to a mile. 22-04-26

runners.comment: Promising Curragh debut second but failed to build on that when favourite at Leopardstown
runners.spotlight: Made 200,000euros as a foal but only 100,000gns as a yearling; promising Curragh debut second but failed to build on that when favourite at Leopardstown; off the track 188 days.

runners.comment: 150-1 for debut and finished last, although beaten only 7l; can only be watched here
runners.spotlight: Not disgraced despite finishing last of six at Leopardstown (sent off 150-1), beaten 7l in a good contest, but can only be watched; 343 days off.

runners.breeder: S A S Elevage Du Haras De Bourgeauville
runners.comment: Intello filly; 17,000euros yearling; half-sister to two winners; tough task on debut
runners.spotlight: Intello filly; 17,000euros yearling; half-sister to winners Dance Of Life (French 10.5f; RPR 89) and Agrimonia (Swiss 1m1f/1m2f); dam 5f 2yo winner (99); tough task on debut.

racecards.verdict: Clearly highly regarded, THE PUBLICAN'S SON can take advatange of his first venture outside of Group company & should be a class apart

runners.comment: Regressive last season but down 14lb and able to drop in grade so don't rule out
runners.spotlight: Won a Ballinrobe claimer last summer but underwhelming subsequently in handicaps for this yard; starts off this season off 14lb lower mark and able to drop in grade so not to be ruled out.

runners.comment: Needs to improve on both recent AW runs
runners.spotlight: Ended last season on a positive note when winning at Tipperary (1m1f, yielding) off 57; two just okay AW runs on last month's return so much more needed on turf return.

runners.comment: Soft ground not ideal on recent Gowran return so more expected back on better ground
runners.spotlight: Ran away with a 7.5f Tipperary handicap last August but wasn't as good raised 13lb at Bellewstown next time; soft ground wasn't ideal on recent Gowran return so more expected back on better ground here.

runners.comment: Recent turf return was a solid run but more required
runners.spotlight: Maiden who has done most of his racing at Dundalk; recent turf return (sixth to Launch Time at Leopardstown, beaten 3.25l) was a solid run but more required.

runners.comment: Lightly raced 5yo very hard to be confident in on seasonal return
runners.spotlight: Very lightly raced 5yo absent since always trailing last of 22 on handicap debut at the Curragh in October; better ground may suit but very hard to be confident in.

runners.comment: Leopardstown winner up 7lb but could well handle it
runners.spotlight: Reappeared a fortnight ago to get off the mark over this trip at Leopardstown in first-time cheekpieces, defying a wide draw to win a shade snugly; 7lb rise a bit harsh but no surprise if he handled it.

quotes.race: Sunday 10th May Leopardstown Family Day Handicap
quotes.quote: I'm very happy with Launch Time. He was placed last year and I thought the cheekpieces might work. He didn't like Dundalk so we just kept him for the turf. Hopefully he'll win another one, I'm delighted to get that. He won't go up much for that. I think there is a 0-60 in Cork for him and we'll see how he is - Cian Hughes, trainer

runners.comment: Recent AW form none too encouraging for this turf return; wide draw a negative
runners.spotlight: Dual Dundalk AW winner is 0-8 on turf and recent AW form none too encouraging for this turf return; wide draw a negative.

runners.comment: Encouraging signs on AW last November; potential improver if handling this shorter trip
runners.spotlight: Maiden showed encouraging signs on AW last November over 1m2f; potential improver back on turf if handling this shorter trip.

runners.comment: Prolific AW winner runner-up in this race last year off 7lb higher so demands respect
runners.spotlight: Recorded his ninth AW win over 1m in November but held of late on same surface; runner-up in this race last year off 7lb higher so demands plenty of respect.

quotes.race: Christmas Party Nights At Dundalk Stadium Handicap
quotes.quote: I let Notforalongtime do what he wanted to do. Coming into the straight, I didn't think he would pick up the way he did and for the last fifty yards I was praying, but he put his head down and worked - Wayne Hassett, speaking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Irishinjuredjockeys.com Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: Notforalongtime had lost his way when I got him and he had a few problems so we were able to sweeten him up. The cheekpieces made a big difference. We'll come up for the winter with him - Laura Hourigan, trainer.

quotes.race: Free Tips Daily On attheraces.com Handicap
quotes.quote: I was chuffed with that, it was a nice enough race and Notforalongtime is a gutsy little horse - Adam Kirby, jockey.

stable_tour.quote: We've gelded him and he's had a wind operation, which can hopefully help him take another step forward. I think he'll continue to progress over a mile and build on his head-bobbing win at Doncaster last summer. 22-04-21

runners.comment: Joined new yard since last run in January and may just need this
runners.spotlight: Four career wins include at Dundalk last November for Gavin Cromwell; joined new yard since last run in January and may just need this.

runners.comment: No success in 17 starts, most at Dundalk; first turf run since August so of limited appeal
runners.spotlight: No success in 17 starts, most at Dundalk; first turf run since last August and of limited appeal.

runners.comment: Decent run here last year at 6f; lacks a recent run so may need this
runners.spotlight: One of her better efforts came here last September when third over 6f; subsequent AW form not at same level; absent since September and may need this.

runners.comment: AW form over the winter wasn't bad so can't be ruled out off a decent mark
runners.spotlight: Three-time AW winner and last of two turf wins came in Roscommon handicap nearly two years ago (off 61); AW form over the winter wasn't bad so can't be ruled out.

quotes.race: Dundalk Stadium Gift Vouchers Available Online Handicap (Div I)
quotes.quote: River Derwent was starting to show a little bit of form of late. Adam (Caffrey) was outstanding on him, it's nice to see him recapture a bit of form. He handled that surface well and we'll keep coming here - Dick Donohoe, trainer, talking to Racing TV.

quotes.race: Foxrock Maiden
quotes.quote: River Derwent is a good looking horse. When he goes up to a mile and a quarter he should be even better. He's a nice horse going forward - Brendan Powell, assistant trainer.

runners.comment: Stiff task on yard debut at Dundalk; blinkers added now and back down to a realistic mark
runners.spotlight: Maiden produced his best effort on final start for the Easterbys when second over 9.5f at Wolverhampton in October off this mark; ran no sort of race on yard debut off a harsh mark of 60 at Dundalk in January; blinkers added now and back down to a realistic mark.

prev_owners.owner: Mrs Lynne Lyons & Sean Jones & David Spratt

runners.comment: Down to basement mark for the first time in his career so worth a look
runners.spotlight: Both turf wins came at this trip on a sound surface; on a long losing run (over 9l off Launch Time at Leopardstown on latest) and down to basement mark for the first time.

quotes.race: Tote Always SP Or Better Handicap
quotes.quote: Hale Bopp, like Bucky Larson is a nice horse to have around the place. Colin said there's a big one in him and he could hit it or miss it depending on the luck of the day - he's that type of horse. I think he's rock solid and could get a mile and two furlongs. He's learning after being immature - Ger Lyons, trainer.

runners.comment: Last seen when second at Killarney; nice mark and good draw so respect
runners.spotlight: Three career wins include over C&D way back; hasn't won in nearly three years but good second on final start last year at Killarney in October when 8lb out of the weights; hard to assess but on a nice mark and good draw.

quotes.race: Torc Waterfall Claiming Race
quotes.quote: Swiss Army Officer was running in big fields at Leopardstown all season and was never beaten far. He needs his own way and he got it. Emmet kidded him along and he won well in the end. These races are probably ideal for him - Kevin Coleman, trainer.

runners.comment: Unexposed 3yo up in trip here and 2lb out of handicap
runners.spotlight: Three Dundalk runs over the winter before handicap/turf debut back in trip at Naas last month, showing up for long way before dropping out; up in trip here and 2lb out of handicap.

runners.comment: Unexposed handicap debutante and yard have a more likely contender in Notforalongtime
runners.spotlight: No impact in a fillies' maiden for Clive Cox last year and hasn't shown much in two runs for current yard this year; handicap debutante is 4lb wrong and yard have a more likely contender in Notforalongtime.

runners.comment: No disgrace in recent turf return; drop in trip may not be in his favour though; reserve
runners.spotlight: First reserve; AW winner in Britain (9.5f); okay form for current yard on AW at end of last year and no disgrace in recent turf return; drop in trip here may not be in his favour though.

runners.comment: Potential improver on turf debut with cheekpieces added; reserve
runners.spotlight: Second reserve; narrow winner of a 6f Dundalk maiden in February but disqualified due to a technicality; okay run on latest of two handicap runs since over same C&D; cheekpieces added for turf debut and interesting if getting a run.

runners.comment: Lots to find with Launch Time on recent turf handicap debut at Leopardstown; reserve
runners.spotlight: Third reserve; lots to find with Launch Time on recent turf handicap debut at Leopardstown.

racecards.verdict: Recent Leopardstown winner LAUNCH TIME could still have more to offer from a 7lb higher mark

runners.comment: Dual-purpose; solid run on the Flat when sixth of 23 at the Curragh in November (heavy)

runners.comment: Third at Clonmel (9.5f) on sole Flat start for Elliott but has struggled for this yard
runners.spotlight: Bumper winner and third at Clonmel (9.5f) on sole Flat start for Gordon Elliott but has struggled in three starts for this yard, including on Flat 15 days ago at Gowran.

quotes.race: Dermot Casey Tree Care Maiden Hurdle
quotes.quote: Eternal Echo got the hang of the jumping and won well so he's a grand horse. I'd say better ground would suit him. He's gone on that ground. We'll see what the owners and Gordon say but I imagine he'll be kept on the go and you'd like to think he could win on the Flat as well. He'll be kept on the go for the summer tracks and we'll see - Ian Amond, assistant Trainer of Gordon Elliott.

quotes.race: Christopher Dunne Memorial (Pro/Am) INH Flat Race
quotes.quote: Eternal Echo is a nice horse and has shown a bit of pace at home. To give the filly a stone was a good performance. He could definitely win on the Flat - Gordon Elliott, trainer.

runners.comment: Soundly beaten both runs over hurdles and similar story in 2 tries on Flat; hard to fancy
runners.spotlight: Second runner for yard; soundly beaten both runs over hurdles and similar story in two tries on Flat; hard to fancy.

runners.comment: Sent off at odds of 50-1 for 9.5f Gowran debut and was never involved; will need more time
runners.spotlight: Sent off at odds of 50-1 for 9.5f Gowran debut this month and was never involved; will need more time.

runners.comment: 18l behind on Flat debut last month; this trip should at least help; watch betting
runners.spotlight: Change of emphasis after Naas bumper run in January; solid Flat pedigree but only modest late headway when 18l behind the winner at Navan (1m) last month; this trip should at least help.

runners.comment: Half-brother to 1m2f winner Alazeyna (RPR 93); dam 1m4f winner (inc Listed); shortlisted
runners.spotlight: Fifth foal; half-brother to 1m2f winner Alazeyna (RPR 93); dam 1m4f winner (inc Listed; 110), half-sister to 1m6f/2m4f Group 1 winner Alandi and 1m4f Listed winner Aliyfa, out of 1m4f Listed winning sister to disqualified Oaks winner Aliysa; Irish Derby entry; shortlisted.

runners.comment: Calyx gelding; 52,000gns yearling; dam 1m2f winner; market the best guide
runners.spotlight: Calyx gelding; 52,000gns yearling; half-brother to Italian 8.7f 2yo winner Ancient Story; dam 1m2f winner (RPR 75), sister to 1m4f/13.5f winner Moon Daisy, half-sister to 7f 2yo Listed winner Mountain Bear; market the best guide.

runners.comment: Two solid runs last year and looks strong form on a line through Cape Cod; every chance
runners.spotlight: Showed plenty of promise when third on his debut at Punchestown (1m1f, yielding to soft) before finishing third at Naas (1m, yielding) in rematch with Cape Cod who won Leopardstown handicap on return off 92 this month; holds Irish Derby entry and entitled to improve up in trip this season.

runners.comment: Tailed off at the Curragh on debut; stable second string on riding arrangements
runners.spotlight: Dwelt coming out of the stalls when tailed off at the Curragh (1m2f) on debut last month; stable second string on riding arrangements.

runners.breeder: His Highness The Aga Khan's Studs S C
